```text
1	# marvin — UI architecture (canvas compositor + per-screen modules)
2	
3	How marvin's operator UI is structured: independently-authored panels (dashboard, nav,
4	dialogs) each render into their own **canvas surface** in RAM, the compositor maps surfaces
5	onto the scarce **LCDC hardware layers**, and — with the MGS screen state machine disabled —
6	the application owns screen orchestration so multiple panels coexist **live and interactive
7	at once** instead of one-screen-at-a-time switching.
8	
9	Read [`spec.md`](spec.md) §4.5 (operator UI) and §4.1 (video/display) first. Decisions in
10	[`journal.md`](journal.md) (2026-06-25). **Status: canvas compositor built and working**
11	(dashboard on BASE + slide-in nav on OVR1, single-active highlight). **Next: the `ui_manager`
12	+ per-screen-module refactor** described in §6–§7.
13	
14	---
15	
16	## 1. The core idea
17	
18	Content geometry was welded to hardware 1:1:1 — one Legato layer → one framebuffer → one LCDC
19	layer. There are only **4 LCDC layers** (`BASE`, `OVR1`, `HEO`, `OVR2`); `HEO` is the live
20	camera. The compositor breaks the welding:
21	
22	- A **surface** is a RAM framebuffer (a GFX Canvas object) holding a panel's pixels.
23	- A **layer** is a hardware compositor window. The LCDC blends them every scan with zero CPU.
24	- Showing a panel = point a layer at its surface + enable (register writes, no re-render).
25	  Hiding = disable/move the layer. Sliding = animate the layer's window position.
26	
27	**GFX Canvas** is the substrate: `GFXC_GetPixelBuffer` redirects Legato's render target to a
28	canvas object, and `gfxcSetLayer`/`ShowCanvas`/`SetWindowPosition` map/show/move that surface
29	on an LCDC layer. (Why canvas and not a hand-rolled retarget or direct-layer-only: see the
30	2026-06-25 journal entry — canvas is the only thing that gets Legato content *into* an
31	arbitrary off-screen surface; direct layer control still does the show/move.)
32	
33	## 2. The enabling change — MGS screen state machine OFF
34	
35	Legato's stock "screen state machine" (`le_gen_init.c`) shows **one screen at a time** —
36	`legato_showScreen` tears down the outgoing screen's widget tree. That is fatal to a compositor
37	that wants several panels live simultaneously. So it is **disabled** ("Generate Screen State
38	Machine" off; `le_gen_init.{c,h}` no longer generated — see the 2026-06-25 journal entry and
39	the `compat/` stub that works around the resulting MGS include bug).
40	
41	Two confirmed facts make this work (verified in `legato_state.c` / `legato_renderer.c` /
42	`legato_input.c`):
43	
44	1. **`_state.layerList` is global and `leUpdate` renders/updates *every* attached layer each
45	   frame.** There is no "active screen" render gate. Attach roots to multiple layers → they all
46	   render live.
47	2. **Touch picks across all attached layers, top-to-bottom** (`leInput` iterates `layerList`
48	   from the top). So an attached overlay is interactive wherever it sits; the layer below
49	   receives touches elsewhere. *(This supersedes the earlier "parked surfaces aren't pickable /
50	   reveal-then-promote" idea — that was a consequence of the state machine, which is now gone.)*
51	
52	So the model is simply: **attach a panel's root to a layer → it is live and interactive;
53	detach (or move off-screen) → it is gone.** No freeze, no promotion dance.
54	
55	## 3. MGS Screen = widget-tree factory
56	
57	With the state machine off, the generated per-screen functions are ours to call directly
58	(MGS even relabels them `// call to show this screen`). We treat each **MGS Screen as a
59	widget-tree factory**, decoupled from display:
60	
61	- `screenInit_X()` — builds the widget tree (+ registers any MGS-wired events).
62	- `screenShow_X()` — attaches its root(s) to layer(s) and raises the `X_OnShow` hook.
63	- `leAddRootWidget(wgt, layer)` / `leRemoveRootWidget(wgt, layer)` — **re-host** a root onto
64	  whatever Legato layer we want, independent of the index MGS authored it on.
65	- `screenGetRoot_X(lyrIdx)` — fetch a root to re-host or toggle visibility.
66	
67	So each panel is authored in its own clean MGS Screen, then the compositor assembles the
68	trees onto the layer set it manages. The screen's `OnShow` hook is that panel's
69	**composition root** — where it runtime-registers its widget event callbacks (the DI pattern;
70	see the 2026-06-25 journal entry on widget events being runtime-registerable while screen
71	lifecycle events are direct calls).
72	
73	## 4. Hardware layer budget
74	
75	| Legato layer | LCDC | Content | Lifecycle |
76	|---|---|---|---|
77	| 0 | BASE | active full-screen view (dashboard, …) | swappable (replace) |
78	| 1 | OVR1 | **nav drawer** | resident — attach once, persists across base-view swaps |
79	| 2 | OVR2 | **modal dialog** (song/mode select), sized to the dialog | shown/hidden; background stays live |
80	| — | HEO | camera | `video.c`, **outside Legato** |
81	
82	- **Nav on its own resident layer ⇒ "same nav over every view" for free** — it is independent
83	  of layer 0, so swapping the base view leaves it untouched.
84	- **Modal dialog on OVR2 sized to the dialog ⇒ uncovered dashboard telemetry keeps updating**
85	  (layer 0 renders live behind it). The dialog is invoked only from the dashboard.
86	- **Ceiling:** dashboard + nav + dialog + camera = **all 4 LCDC layers**. A 4th simultaneous UI
87	  surface needs canvas multiplexing (`gfxcSetBaseCanvasID`) or giving up a layer.
88	
89	### 4.1 Two layer counts — don't conflate them
90	- **`LE_LAYER_COUNT`** (Legato, `legato_config.h`) = how many canvases / Legato layers the global
91	  `layerList` manages = **3**. MGS derives it as the **max layer count across all screens** in the
92	  design; there is no explicit knob.
93	- **`XLCDC_TOT_LAYERS`** (XLCDC driver, "Total Layers" in `le_gfx_driver_xlcdc.yml`) = enumerated
94	  hardware layers = **4** (`layerOrder` = {BASE 0, HEO 1, OVR1 2, OVR2 3}).
95	
96	They differ on purpose: Legato manages 3 canvases, each mapped onto **3 of the 4** hardware layers.
97	
98	### 4.2 Pinning `LE_LAYER_COUNT` = 3 (the LayerBudget screen)
99	Each panel is authored as its own **1-layer** MGS screen, so nothing reaches 3 layers on its own —
100	and there's no direct setting. A dedicated, **never-shown `LayerBudget` screen with 3 layers** pins
101	the count (regen-safe; no `legato_config.h` patch). Keep it un-shown: its roots then never attach,
102	so Legato layer 2 stays an empty internal root. **Caveat:** `LE_LAYER_COUNT` 3 lets Legato render
103	into `canvas[2]`, whose buffer is still the generated `NULL` until the dialog assigns one — safe
104	**only** while layer 2 has no attached root / no damage (i.e. LayerBudget is never shown and no panel
105	re-hosts onto layer 2 yet).
106	
107	### 4.3 Why HEO is safe (and stays enabled)
108	Layer targeting is **explicit, not positional**: Legato layer *i* → `canvas[i]` →
109	`gfxcSetLayer(i, hwLayer)`, where `hwLayer` indexes `layerOrder`. We map canvases only to hw layers
110	**0 / 2 / 3** (BASE / OVR1 / OVR2) and **never to 1 (HEO)**, so the canvas framework never issues an
111	IOCTL to HEO regardless of enumeration order. The only GFX-side touch of HEO is
112	`DRV_XLCDC_Initialize` disabling all enumerated layers once at init — before `video.c` configures it
113	(post-scheduler), so video is the last writer. So **HEO stays enabled** and `video.c` keeps full
114	runtime control via the XLCDC PLIB, including the `HEOCFG12` blender + `VIDPRI` z-order that
115	`XLCDC_SetupHEOLayer` provides (`video.c` does not set those itself — which is exactly why disabling
116	HEO in MCC would break compositing, and why we don't).
117	
118	## 5. Live coexistence vs. replacement
119	
120	The compositor offers two verbs, chosen per interaction — you do **not** pick one global mode:
121	
122	- **Coexist (overlay-as-layer)** — the panel is its own layer over a still-live background.
123	  Used for the **nav drawer** (dashboard keeps updating behind it) and the **modal dialog**
124	  (telemetry keeps updating around it). No freeze.
125	- **Replace (switch base view)** — a full-screen view replaces another on layer 0; the
126	  outgoing one detaches (its surface can hold the last frame, or it is rebuilt on return).
127	  Used when a view genuinely supersedes the dashboard and live background isn't needed.
128	
129	Because the compositor owns layer placement and attach/detach, moving an interaction between
130	these is a compositor-level change, not a per-module rewrite — the reversibility we wanted.
131	
132	## 6. Module structure
133	
134	```
135	            ┌──────────────────────── ui_manager ─────────────────────────┐
136	            │ string-table init · screen init/show · root re-host onto     │
137	            │ layers · layer/canvas pool · visibility · verbs:             │
138	            │   show_view(X) · push_overlay(nav|dialog) · hide_overlay(…)   │
139	            └───────┬──────────────────────┬───────────────────────┬───────┘
140	              ┌─────▼─────┐          ┌──────▼──────┐          ┌──────▼──────┐
141	              │ui/dashboard│         │   ui/nav    │          │ui/song_select│
142	              │ (BASE,lyr0)│         │ (OVR1,lyr1) │          │ (OVR2,lyr2)  │
143	              └────────────┘         └─────────────┘          └──────────────┘
144	   each: owns its widgets + interactions; composition root = its screen OnShow hook
145	```
146	
147	- **`ui_manager`** (promoted from today's `compositor.c`) owns the *mechanism*: string-table
148	  setup, calling `screenInit_/screenShow_`, re-hosting roots onto the right layer, the canvas
149	  buffer pool, layer visibility, and the coexist/replace verbs. It is the "top-level module
150	  that ties everything together."
151	- **Per-screen/overlay modules** own only their panel's content + event wiring, registered
152	  from their own `OnShow` composition root. They never call `legato_*`/canvas APIs directly —
153	  they go through `ui_manager`, which is what keeps the layer mechanics swappable.
154	
155	## 7. Build state & refactor plan
156	
157	**Built (committed):** GFX Canvas substrate; state machine off + app-owned `screenInit/Show`
158	(`compat/le_gen_init.h` stub); `ui_manager` orchestrator + dashboard on BASE; `LE_LAYER_COUNT`=3
159	pinned via the never-shown `LayerBudget` screen (§4.2). **Nav drawer is feature-complete:** its
160	own `Navigation` MGS Screen re-hosted onto OVR1; slide in/out via canvas Move FX (Move FX
161	re-enabled; `NAV_CLOSED_X` dodges the window-clip row-wrap; mid-slide reversal cancels the
162	in-flight move); single-active highlight via a runtime-registered shared release sink (Dashboard
163	closes, others switch); full-repaint-on-open; rounded buttons (set in code; not AA — §10).
164	
165	**Next:**
166	1. **Author song/mode-select as its own MGS Screen;** assign `canvas[2]` a real buffer and have
167	   `ui_manager` host it on layer 2 (OVR2) as a modal (sized to the dialog, dashboard live behind).
168	   First real exercise of the coexist verb with a *live* background; the re-host + slide
169	   mechanics are proven on the nav.
170	2. **`manual_input.c` fate** — `Screen0` is retired, but the strum handlers now serve the
171	   Dashboard screen, so `manual_input.c` stays until manual control is reworked.
172	
173	## 8. Static-allocation, cache & priority rules
174	
175	- **Static non-cached surfaces.** Each canvas surface is a file-scope static array in
176	  `.region_nocache` (no malloc), passed via `gfxcSetPixelBuffer`. They are CPU-rendered then
177	  read by the 2D engine / LCDC DMA, so non-cached is required (same policy as `FB_CACHE_NC`
178	  and the Legato scratch — 2026-06-24 cache-coherency fix). RGB565 to match the panel.
179	- **`GFX_CANVAS_Task`** is at UI-band priority 2 (set in the gfx_canvas yml), required even
180	  with FX off (drives `INIT→RUNNING`). It's a dynamic MCC task on heap_1 like the others.
181	- **Heap.** The canvas component pushed `heap_1` past 40 KB → silent boot hang via the
182	  malloc-failed hook; heap is now 65536 and the fault hooks emit a DBGU marker (2026-06-25).
183	
184	## 9. Memory budget
185	
186	`.region_nocache` is 32 MB, shared with the ISC capture pool (~10.5 MB) + Legato scratch
187	(0.5 MB). Full-screen RGB565 surface ≈ 2.0 MB; overlays sized to content are far less (nav
188	~320×800 ≈ 0.5 MB; a modal dialog smaller still). ~19 MB free after BASE + capture + scratch,
189	so **memory is not the binding constraint — the 3 UI layers are.**
190	
191	## 10. Open items
192	
193	- **Base-view replacement** detail when a 2nd full-screen view arrives (rebuild vs parked
194	  last-frame on return; how nav persistence interacts with `screenShow`/`Hide` of layer 0).
195	- **`manual_input.c` fate** — `Screen0` retired; the strum handlers now serve the Dashboard
196	  screen, so it stays until manual control is reworked.
197	- **Per-pixel alpha** — which (if any) overlay needs ARGB8888 over the camera vs. layer alpha.
198	
199	## 10a. Anti-aliased rounded button corners (done)
200	
201	The nav buttons use the widget `cornerRadius` (set in code — not exposed in MGS), but the
202	classic skin's rounded-rect fill draws corners with `leRenderer_ArcFill` (hard, stepped
203	edges). Smoothing is done **without touching Legato/MCC code** (`config/default/` is
204	off-limits), via a per-instance vtable re-point in `src/ui/button_aa.c`:
205	
206	- `leWidget.fn` is a writable per-instance pointer to a `const` vtable. `ButtonAA_Enable`
207	  makes one shared writable copy of the button vtable, overrides only `_paint`, and points
208	  the button's `fn`/`widget.fn` at it. No `LE_DYNAMIC_VTABLES` (not an MCC knob; unguarded
209	  `#define 0` in generated `legato_config.h`), no global RAM cost — scoped to re-pointed
210	  buttons.
211	- The wrapper runs the original paint (bg + label + border), then on `DONE` with the
212	  supported radius overdraws the four corners: sample the backdrop from each corner's
213	  extreme pixel (left untouched by the rounded fill), then blend a 1px transition band from
214	  a precomputed coverage mask via `leColorLerp` + `leRenderer_PutPixel`. Fill is read from
215	  the live scheme each paint, so highlight (selected/unselected) and pressed states track.
216	- Runs **in-pass** (damage → repaint → AA in one paint), so no timing/flicker window.
217	- Wired from `nav_buttons_init()`; currently nav-only. Extending app-wide is just calling
218	  `ButtonAA_Enable` from other screens' button init. Single radius (`BUTTON_AA_RADIUS`);
219	  other radii pass through unsmoothed.
220	
221	## 11. Relationship to spec §4.5 / Q5
222	
223	This answers spec **Q5** (Legato vs. custom UI) for the *presentation* layer: **Legato is the
224	renderer; a marvin `ui_manager` over GFX Canvas owns surface/layer composition and screen
225	orchestration.** Per-screen *authoring* stays in MGS (one Screen per panel); the compositor
226	assembles their trees onto hardware layers.

1	# marvin — Working Journal
2	
3	Running log of planning, decisions, open questions, and work-in-progress for marvin. Newest entries at the top. For *what marvin is* (purpose, subsystems, interfaces, milestones), read [`spec.md`](spec.md) — this journal does not duplicate it.
4	
5	---
6	
7	**UI architecture — nav drawer complete; song/mode-select dialog is the next UI step.** The canvas compositor + per-screen-module model is built and validated on hardware: `ui_manager` orchestrates screens (string table + `screenInit/Show`; the MGS screen state machine is disabled, worked around with the `compat/le_gen_init.h` stub), the dashboard is its own MGS Screen on BASE, and the nav drawer is its own MGS Screen (`Navigation`) re-hosted onto OVR1 — they coexist live (no active-screen gate; `leUpdate`/`leInput` cover all attached layers). `LE_LAYER_COUNT`=3 is pinned via the never-shown `LayerBudget` screen. **Nav drawer is feature-complete:** slides in/out via canvas Move FX (`NAV_CLOSED_X` dodges the window-clip row-wrap; mid-slide reversal cancels the in-flight move), single-active highlight (Dashboard closes, others switch), clean close, rounded buttons with anti-aliased corners (`ui/button_aa.c`, per-instance vtable re-point — see `ui_compositor.md` §10a). Authoritative design + the window-clip/alignment gotchas in [`ui_compositor.md`](ui_compositor.md); decisions 2026-06-25. **Next:** author song/mode-select as its own MGS Screen, hosted by `ui_manager` on OVR2 as a modal (assign `canvas[2]` a buffer, re-host onto layer 2, dashboard live behind) — first coexist-with-live-background exercise; the re-host + slide mechanics are proven on the nav. Ties into the song_list widget below (the scrollable list goes inside that dialog). The earlier "parked surfaces aren't pickable / reveal-then-promote" framing is **superseded** (a state-machine artifact).
8	
9	**Song-select operator UI — scrollable list widget built & validated on hardware.** Custom Legato widget `ui/song_list.{h,c}` (a hand-written `leWidget` subclass) renders the SELECT SONG setlist (tier badge + bold title + dim artist + right-aligned duration), driven by a decoupled row-provider callback (no catalog dependency); drag-scroll with time-based kinetic inertia, tap-to-select. Bring-up via the `songlist` console command + a catalog-backed demo provider (`ui/song_list_demo.{c,h}`) — scroll/select/opaque-fill confirmed on hardware. **Bringing it up surfaced and fixed a real Legato/GFX2D cache-coherency bug** (see decision log 2026-06-24): the CPU-rendered scratch buffer was cacheable, so the 2D-engine blit leaked stale pixels through opaque widgets — fixed by placing the scratch in non-cached DDR. **Next:** author the full SELECT SONG screen in MGS (album art + catalog-fed metadata panel + difficulty/mode/Select), and the **tier / career-setlist data model** (the `tier` badge needs the deferred catalog tier column). Two upstream Microchip Legato/gfx bugs to file (decision log).
10	
11	**Song catalog loader — built and committed; exercised on hardware via the `catalog`/`songlist` console commands.** New `game/catalog.{h,c}` maps the recognizer's `(setlist, index)` → human labels (title/artist/bpm/length) from `<card>/games/gh3-wii/songs.csv`, so the UI/high-score display shows names instead of `#4`. Flat **CSV** (decided over the spec's JSON for the same reasons `results` is CSV — no on-device tokenizer, `FF_FS_MAX_FILES=1`, static buffers, pandas/Excel-editable). The two CSV helpers were extracted out of `results.c` into a shared `util/csv.{h,c}` and the catalog reuses them. Lazy-loads once into a fixed `[GP_N_SONGS]` static cache (file closed after load), so lookups are O(n) in RAM and don't fight `results.csv` for the single FatFs handle. `catalog` console command (`reload` / `ls` / `<main|bonus> <index>`) validates the path against a checked-in seed catalog (`data/games/gh3-wii/songs.csv`). Columns: `setlist,index,title,artist,album,bpm,length_s,year,genre,difficulty`. `title`/`artist`/`album` are real, sourced from the `SONGS` table in `tools/fetch_gh3_cover_art.py` (incl. proper UTF-8 — *Héroes del Silencio*, *Mauvais Garçon*); that script gained a `--catalog` mode that also fills `year`/`genre` from MusicBrainz on a networked run. `bpm`/`length_s`/`difficulty` are reserved-but-blank (GH3 surfaces no per-song difficulty; the authentic signal is the career tier, deferred). Catalog is labels only: a missing/stale card degrades to "Unknown song" and never touches recognition (compile-time in flash). **Deferred:** the stale-catalog version warning — `export_c.py` doesn't emit `GP_METADATA_VERSION` yet (open item below). **Next SD consumer:** album-artwork pre-cache (spec §4.8.7) — directory structure is now locked (`art/{small,large}/<setlist>-<NN>.{jpg,png}`, one size-tier subdir per DDR cache), marvin decode side not yet built.
12	
13	**T1S inter-node link — built and working (marvin ↔ guitar).** marvin is the PLCA **coordinator** (node 0) on a 10BASE-T1S bus (LAN8651 over FLEXCOM4 SPI); hand-authored stack in `default/src/net/t1s/`. It sends the actuator command over T1S to the `guitar` follower node (id 2), which actuates the Wii GPIOs (guitar G1+G2 proven). Followers announce presence via a heartbeat (ethertype `0x88B6`); the `t1s` and `nodes` console commands report link/credits/per-node presence. Transport is behind `MARVIN_FRETBOARD_TRANSPORT={UART,T1S}` (T1S default on the `t1s` branch). The `fretboard` node (id 1) firmware is now **written, T1S-only** (fretboard journal 2026-06-17): it streams its 17-byte frame to marvin **and** drives the `guitar` node directly — its on-device model infers the bitmask and sends it peer-to-peer to `02:..:02`. marvin's RX side needed no changes — `fretboard_link.c`'s T1S frame handler already parses the frame from node id 1 (`DETECTOR_ADC_FRETBOARD`) and the node-table + heartbeat-presence demux already cover it. **Next (marvin side):** **active-source arbitration** — both marvin (timing pipeline) and the fretboard now address the guitar (`02:..:02`), so marvin needs active-detector/active-guitar selection to ensure exactly one source drives at a time (the fretboard's SW0 is an interim manual arm; until then, don't run marvin's timing pipeline to the guitar while the fretboard is armed). Then fretboard hardware bring-up. PoDL is design-direction only. Detail in [`../../../docs/t1s-podl-link.md`](../../../docs/t1s-podl-link.md); decision log entry 2026-06-17.
14	
15	**Board port: SAM9X75 Curiosity → Curiosity Hybrid (in progress).** USB Host is gone on the Hybrid; the fretboard link was rewired from USB CDC host to a direct FLEXCOM2 USART on 2026-06-08 (see decision log + session log). Code-complete and syntax-checked; pending a full MPLAB build and on-hardware bring-up. Display/MIPI I²C (incl. TC358743 control) also moved off FLEXCOM6/PA24-PA25 to FLEXCOM8 TWI/PB4-PB5 during the port — `spec.md` §3.1/§3.2 reconciled on 2026-06-08. Dated 2026-05-01/05-20 journal entries and `journal-archive.md` keep their FLEXCOM6 references as historical record (true on the original Curiosity board).
16	
17	**M1 — Reference detector v0.** First CV detector running on captured frames, publishing `detector_state_t` records onto the detector-state bus. No actuation yet. See [`spec.md`](spec.md) §4.2 for subsystem detail and §8 for the milestone progression.
18

Next: pick the v0 algorithm (Q8) and start populating `fret[]`.

32	## Decision log
33	
34	| Date | Decision | Rationale |
35	|------|----------|-----------|
36	| 2026-06-26 | **Anti-aliased rounded button corners via a per-instance vtable re-point — no Legato/MCC edits (`ui/button_aa.c`).** The classic skin draws rounded corners with `leRenderer_ArcFill` (hard stepped edges). `ButtonAA_Enable(btn)` makes one shared writable copy of the button vtable, overrides only `_paint`, and points the button's `fn`/`widget.fn` at the copy; the wrapper runs the original paint then, on `DONE` at the supported radius, overdraws the four corners — sampling each corner's extreme (untouched) pixel as backdrop and blending a 1px band from a precomputed coverage mask (`leColorLerp` + `leRenderer_PutPixel`). Wired from `nav_buttons_init()` (nav-only for now; extend by adding call sites). Also added a CLAUDE.md rule: do not modify MCC-generated/Legato code under `config/default/`. Design in [`ui_compositor.md`](ui_compositor.md) §10a. | Editing the skin (the obvious spot) is forbidden — it's vendor/MCC code that regen silently overwrites. `LE_DYNAMIC_VTABLES` (the sanctioned global override) is **not** an MCC knob and is an unguarded `#define 0` in generated `legato_config.h` (can't flip via config, can't `-D`, can't hand-edit) — dead end. A post-render overdraw on the nav canvas has no vendor-legal post-paint hook and fights Legato's damage-repaint (1-frame hard-corner flash). The per-instance re-point exploits that `leWidget.fn` is a *writable* pointer to a const vtable: it needs no config flag, costs one vtable struct + one mask in BSS (static-allocation discipline holds), runs **in-pass** (repaint→AA same paint, no timing window), and is scoped to exactly the buttons we re-point. **Confirmed on hardware** — smooth corners across selected/unselected/pressed states and slide cycles. |
37	| 2026-06-25 | **Re-enabled GFX Canvas Move FX to animate the nav drawer slide (reverses the earlier "FX off, do our own" call).** The nav drawer now slides in/out by animating its OVR1 canvas window position via `gfxcStartEffectMove` (DEC ease-out), rather than snapping. With a concrete slide need this is the textbook canvas-move case (the doc flagged it as where canvas FX earns its weight); rolling our own would just duplicate the FX timer + `GFX_CANVAS_Task` we already have, and the FX timer only ticks during an active move (no steady cost). Open slides −off→0; entry taps switch the highlight (Dashboard also closes); a move-done callback (`nav_fx_done`) disables OVR1 when a close finishes. **Window-clip gotcha (cost a few iterations):** a canvas layer can't sit truly off-screen — the clip emulates negative X by shifting the source pointer + shrinking the window, but it first aligns X *down* to a multiple of 4 (`x &= ~0x3`, non-32bpp) and wraps a row once \|X\| hits the surface width, briefly flashing the panel's left columns; and the layer update busy-waits for the vsync latch, so that bad frame displays before the hide. Fix: slide to the furthest 4-aligned X with \|X\| < NAV_W (`NAV_CLOSED_X`, derived from NAV_W — not a magic number) so the final shown frame is an in-bounds edge sliver, then `nav_fx_done` disables the layer to clear it. | Canvas Move FX over a hand-rolled stepper because the machinery already exists (just was disabled) and it's purpose-built for sliding a layer window with easing; the earlier FX-off decision was speculative (pre-slide). The off-screen constant is derived + documented (points at the exact clip line) rather than hard-coded, accepting a documented coupling to the generated canvas clip — same class as the cache/scratch and HEO-blender couplings. Full decoupling (own the slide via direct XLCDC position stepping) is the fallback if the clip bites again. |
38	| 2026-06-25 | **UI architecture: disable the MGS screen state machine and let the app own screen orchestration, so panels coexist as live, independently-interactive LCDC layers — `ui_manager` + per-screen modules. Authoritative design in [`ui_compositor.md`](ui_compositor.md).** Confirmed in the Legato core that `_state.layerList` is global, `leUpdate` renders/updates **every** attached layer each frame, and `leInput` picks touch across **all** attached layers top-to-bottom — there is no "active screen" render/pick gate. The only thing enforcing one-screen-at-a-time was `le_gen_init.c`'s state machine (`legato_showScreen` tears down the outgoing tree). Turning it off (and working around the MGS dangling-`le_gen_init.h` bug with a `compat/` stub) means we attach multiple panels' roots to different layers and they're all live + interactive at once. **Model:** each panel is authored as its own MGS Screen used as a *widget-tree factory* (`screenInit_` builds, `screenShow_` attaches + raises its `OnShow` composition root); `leAddRootWidget`/`leRemoveRootWidget` re-host a root onto whatever layer we choose. Layers: dashboard=BASE/0, nav=OVR1/1 (resident → "same nav over every view" free), modal song/mode dialog=OVR2/2 (sized to the dialog so live dashboard telemetry shows around it); camera=HEO outside Legato. Two verbs — **coexist** (overlay-as-layer, background live) and **replace** (swap base view on layer 0) — chosen per interaction, both owned by `ui_manager`, so the choice is reversible. `compositor.c` is promoted to `ui_manager`; per-screen/overlay modules own only their widgets+wiring. **This supersedes the earlier "parked surfaces aren't pickable / reveal-then-promote" idea in the doc** — that was a symptom of the state machine, now removed. | Greg's call to author nav + dialogs as separate MGS Screens (cleaner than overlapping layers in one Screen) collided with Legato's one-active-screen model; the resolution was to drop that model entirely rather than fight it, which the global-layerList facts make safe. Disabling the state machine also removes MGS's per-screen switch baggage outright (deleted code, not dormant) and hands us `screenInit/Show` directly. Live-coexistence (vs. freeze) was required because some dashboard telemetry must keep updating under the nav/dialog (the camera already self-updates on HEO). Per-screen modules + a `ui_manager` orchestrator keep each panel's wiring local (composition-root-per-screen) while one top-level module owns the scarce layer budget — matching the MCC-isolation idiom (own files via `user.cmake`). 3 UI layers + camera is the hard ceiling. | 
39	| 2026-06-25 | **The GFX Canvas regen pushed FreeRTOS `heap_1` past 40 KB → silent boot hang (zero DBGU output); raised `configTOTAL_HEAP_SIZE` 40960 → 100000.** Symptom: after the canvas MCC commit (`ed54f37`), marvin produced no DBGU output at all — bisected to that commit (`8de7c64` working). Not the compositor (it was stashed), and not the XLCDC OVR setup (BASE/HEO use the identical `LCDC_ATTRE`/`WAIT_ATTRS_EQ(SIP)` pre-`Start` pattern that already works, so OVR is symmetric). I now have the full picture. Key facts that shape the reorg:

- The include root is `default/src`, so every UI header is included as `ui/<name>.h`. Moving files into subfolders changes those include paths (e.g. `ui/nav.h` → `ui/nav/nav.h`) — I'll need to fix include sites in `nav.c`, `ui_manager.c`, `song_list_demo.c`, `app.c`, and `console.c`, plus the `user.cmake` source list. No new include directory is needed.
- The current `ui/` files split into three roles: **orchestrator** (`ui_manager`), **screens/panels** (`nav`; `manual_input` is the input shim for the MGS-generated Dashboard), and **reusable widgets** (`song_list` + its `song_list_demo` bring-up provider, `button_aa`).

There are a couple of reasonable ways to lay this out, and since this sets a convention future screens will follow, let me confirm the structure before moving anything.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-26 14:59:51Z)**_

<tool-use data-tool-type="generic" data-tool-name="AskUserQuestion"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **AskUserQuestion**</summary>
**How should I lay out default/src/ui/? (ui_manager stays at the ui/ root as the orchestrator in all options.)**

Options:
- **Screens + widgets split** - Group by role: screens/ for panels, widgets/ for reusable widgets. Clearest long-term intent; new screens drop into screens/.
- **Flat per-thing folders** - One folder per screen/widget directly under ui/, as you described. Simplest; no extra nesting level.
- **Screens foldered, widgets flat** - Each screen gets a folder; widgets stay as files at ui/ root (or one widgets/ folder). Minimal churn for the small widget files.

**Where should manual_input.c go? It's the app-side input shim for the MGS-generated Dashboard screen (the Dashboard widget tree itself lives in config/default/).**

Options:
- **dashboard/ screen folder** - Treat it as the Dashboard screen's module (dashboard/manual_input.c). Consistent with nav being its own screen folder.
- **Leave at ui/ root** - Keep manual_input.c flat at ui/ root since the rest of the Dashboard is MGS-generated and there's only one app-side file.
- **Rename to dashboard/dashboard_input.c** - Move into dashboard/ AND rename so the filename matches the screen. More churn but clearer naming.


**Answer:** I think first option (screens/ and widgets/) but let's also be more explicit with module naming. for example screen_nav and widget_song_list, leave it at root for the moment. The dashboard doesn't use this anymore but we will eventually be creating a manual input screen that will use it. we'll deal with at that time
</details></tool-use>

17	 * select handler. Painted virtualized — only visible rows are drawn, via the
18	 * Legato renderer (no per-row child widgets).
19	 *
20	 * Allocated from the Legato widget pool like every MGS widget (one
21	 * self-contained allocation; all state lives in the widget struct). Attach with
22	 * the usual parent->fn->addChild(parent, SongList_New()); Legato owns its
23	 * lifetime and frees it on screen teardown. */

7:**UI architecture — nav drawer complete; song/mode-select dialog is the next UI step.** The canvas compositor + per-screen-module model is built and validated on hardware: `ui_manager` orchestrates screens (string table + `screenInit/Show`; the MGS screen state machine is disabled, worked around with the `compat/le_gen_init.h` stub), the dashboard is its own MGS Screen on BASE, and the nav drawer is its own MGS Screen (`Navigation`) re-hosted onto OVR1 — they coexist live (no active-screen gate; `leUpdate`/`leInput` cover all attached layers). `LE_LAYER_COUNT`=3 is pinned via the never-shown `LayerBudget` screen. **Nav drawer is feature-complete:** slides in/out via canvas Move FX (`NAV_CLOSED_X` dodges the window-clip row-wrap; mid-slide reversal cancels the in-flight move), single-active highlight (Dashboard closes, others switch), clean close, rounded buttons with anti-aliased corners (`ui/button_aa.c`, per-instance vtable re-point — see `ui_compositor.md` §10a). Authoritative design + the window-clip/alignment gotchas in [`ui_compositor.md`](ui_compositor.md); decisions 2026-06-25. **Next:** author song/mode-select as its own MGS Screen, hosted by `ui_manager` on OVR2 as a modal (assign `canvas[2]` a buffer, re-host onto layer 2, dashboard live behind) — first coexist-with-live-background exercise; the re-host + slide mechanics are proven on the nav. Ties into the song_list widget below (the scrollable list goes inside that dialog). The earlier "parked surfaces aren't pickable / reveal-then-promote" framing is **superseded** (a state-machine artifact).
9:**Song-select operator UI — scrollable list widget built & validated on hardware.** Custom Legato widget `ui/song_list.{h,c}` (a hand-written `leWidget` subclass) renders the SELECT SONG setlist (tier badge + bold title + dim artist + right-aligned duration), driven by a decoupled row-provider callback (no catalog dependency); drag-scroll with time-based kinetic inertia, tap-to-select. Bring-up via the `songlist` console command + a catalog-backed demo provider (`ui/song_list_demo.{c,h}`) — scroll/select/opaque-fill confirmed on hardware. **Bringing it up surfaced and fixed a real Legato/GFX2D cache-coherency bug** (see decision log 2026-06-24): the CPU-rendered scratch buffer was cacheable, so the 2D-engine blit leaked stale pixels through opaque widgets — fixed by placing the scratch in non-cached DDR. **Next:** author the full SELECT SONG screen in MGS (album art + catalog-fed metadata panel + difficulty/mode/Select), and the **tier / career-setlist data model** (the `tier` badge needs the deferred catalog tier column). Two upstream Microchip Legato/gfx bugs to file (decision log).
36:| 2026-06-26 | **Anti-aliased rounded button corners via a per-instance vtable re-point — no Legato/MCC edits (`ui/button_aa.c`).** The classic skin draws rounded corners with `leRenderer_ArcFill` (hard stepped edges). `ButtonAA_Enable(btn)` makes one shared writable copy of the button vtable, overrides only `_paint`, and points the button's `fn`/`widget.fn` at the copy; the wrapper runs the original paint then, on `DONE` at the supported radius, overdraws the four corners — sampling each corner's extreme (untouched) pixel as backdrop and blending a 1px band from a precomputed coverage mask (`leColorLerp` + `leRenderer_PutPixel`). Wired from `nav_buttons_init()` (nav-only for now; extend by adding call sites). Also added a CLAUDE.md rule: do not modify MCC-generated/Legato code under `config/default/`. Design in [`ui_compositor.md`](ui_compositor.md) §10a. | Editing the skin (the obvious spot) is forbidden — it's vendor/MCC code that regen silently overwrites. `LE_DYNAMIC_VTABLES` (the sanctioned global override) is **not** an MCC knob and is an unguarded `#define 0` in generated `legato_config.h` (can't flip via config, can't `-D`, can't hand-edit) — dead end. A post-render overdraw on the nav canvas has no vendor-legal post-paint hook and fights Legato's damage-repaint (1-frame hard-corner flash). The per-instance re-point exploits that `leWidget.fn` is a *writable* pointer to a const vtable: it needs no config flag, costs one vtable struct + one mask in BSS (static-allocation discipline holds), runs **in-pass** (repaint→AA same paint, no timing window), and is scoped to exactly the buttons we re-point. **Confirmed on hardware** — smooth corners across selected/unselected/pressed states and slide cycles. |
41:| 2026-06-25 | **Operator-UI presentation layer = a marvin compositor over the GFX Canvas component: pre-render UI panels into static non-cached RAM surfaces, multiplex the two free LCDC overlay layers (`OVR1`/`OVR2`) across them. Design captured in [`ui_compositor.md`](ui_compositor.md).** The goal is to bring a panel up (or slide it in) instantly without re-rendering or redrawing what's behind it. Confirmed the enabling fact in code: Legato's only "where do I render" knob is the active layer's `pixelBuffer.pixels` (it paints a scratch buffer, then `DRV_XLCDC_BlitBuffer` copies into `drvLayer[activeLayer].pixelBuffer`); there is **no** stock Legato API to render a widget tree into an arbitrary off-screen buffer. **GFX Canvas is exactly that missing indirection** — `GFXC_GetPixelBuffer` hands Legato a canvas object's buffer and `gfxcSetBaseCanvasID` switches which canvas a layer renders into, with `gfxcSetLayer`/show/hide/position/alpha + fade/move on top. Layer budget: `BASE`=background, `OVR1`/`OVR2`=swappable overlays (to be enabled — `XLCDC_TOT_LAYERS` is 2 today), `HEO`=live camera (off-limits). Legato stays the **renderer** (fonts, `song_list`); a thin `ui/` compositor owns surface↔layer multiplexing. Touch handled by **reveal-then-promote** (parked surfaces are non-interactive; promote to a live Legato layer to interact). Phased plan P0–P5 + open questions in the doc. **Design only — no code/MCC yet.** | Reverses the earlier "back off canvas" — that call was made on the **wrong axis**: canvas was dismissed for the *slide animation* (which direct `XLCDC_SetLayerWindowXYPos` stepping handles fine, no framework needed), but the actual problem is the **off-screen surface pool** (render content decoupled from a hardware layer), and that is canvas's literal reason to exist. The two homegrown alternatives lose: DIY pixel-buffer retarget reimplements canvas's per-surface/scratch/binding bookkeeping (~half of canvas, growing once surfaces aren't full-screen); direct-layer-only can present/animate but can't get Legato content *into* a surface. Canvas's earlier objections are addressable, not fatal: it deletes the static `frame_buffer` array, but we *use* the canvas buffers as our surfaces (statically allocated, non-cached per the 2026-06-24 fix), so static-allocation holds; the dynamic `GFX_CANVAS_Task` converts to `xTaskCreateStatic` or rides alongside the existing MCC dynamic tasks. Binding constraint is **layers (2 free), not memory** (~21 MB free in the 32 MB `ram_nocache` after the ISC pool + scratch; full-screen RGB565 ≈ 2 MB, most overlays far less). Resolves spec Q5 for the *presentation* layer (Legato renderer + canvas compositor) without dictating per-screen authoring. |
43:| 2026-06-24 | **Song-select setlist = a hand-written custom Legato widget (`leWidget` subclass), not the stock list widget.** `ui/song_list.{h,c}`: subclass with overridden `_paint`/`update`/touch handlers. Stock `leListWidget` is disabled **and** its item model (icon + one string) can't render the tier-badge + two-line + right-aligned-duration row. Design: **row-provider callback** `songlist_row_fn` (widget never includes `game/catalog.h`; the screen owns catalog→row mapping + future tier grouping); **drag + kinetic inertia** computed from the **FreeRTOS tick** (`leUpdate(0)` means the framework `dt` is always 0, so the widget measures real elapsed time itself for frame-rate-independent motion); **tap-to-select** (<10 px movement) with a selection callback; **virtualized software paint** (`leRenderer_RectFill` + `leStringRenderer_DrawCString`, visible rows only, no per-row child widgets); single **pool allocation** with the vtable built by **copying the base vtable at runtime** (project builds `LE_DYNAMIC_VTABLES=0`, so `_leWidget_FillVTable` isn't linkable and the GenerateVTable path is compiled out); declared **opaque** (`BACKGROUND_FILL`) so Legato composites it. Lives entirely in `ui/` (added via `user.cmake`) — zero edits to the generated `gfx/legato/` tree. Bring-up: `ui/song_list_demo.{c,h}` + a `songlist` console command (`attach`/`off`/`hide`/`show`/`solid`/`tree`/`stats`) with a catalog-backed provider; **validated on hardware**. | Matches the project's MCC-isolation idiom (own module + `user.cmake`, like `console`/`perf_log`); the widget is the primary, reusable piece, so it was built first, ahead of the MGS screen around it. Row-provider keeps the widget generic and testable and lets the screen map `Catalog_At(i)` → row (and supply tier badges once the tier column exists). Pool allocation (not static) because Legato recursively `LE_FREE`s the whole child tree on screen teardown (`legato_widget.c`) — a static widget attached to a screen would feed a static pointer to `LE_FREE`; the Legato widget pool is the accepted heap carve-out, and the widget is one self-contained allocation (fixed internal scratch, no secondary mallocs). Time-based inertia (vs per-tick) because the update cadence is render-bound (~55 Hz) and irregular under the priority-2 UI task. Tier badges blank until the deferred catalog `tier` column lands. |
209:- **Module split.** `compositor.c` → `ui_manager` (orchestrator) + `ui/nav`. Nav became its own `Navigation` MGS Screen re-hosted onto OVR1 via `leRemoveRootWidget`/`leAddRootWidget` — the "MGS Screen as widget-tree factory" model. Renamed the main screen Marvin → Dashboard, retired `Screen0`. `LE_LAYER_COUNT`=3 pinned by a never-shown `LayerBudget` screen.
```

132	## 6. Module structure
133	
134	```
135	            ┌──────────────────────── ui_manager ─────────────────────────┐
136	            │ string-table init · screen init/show · root re-host onto     │
137	            │ layers · layer/canvas pool · visibility · verbs:             │
138	            │   show_view(X) · push_overlay(nav|dialog) · hide_overlay(…)   │
139	            └───────┬──────────────────────┬───────────────────────┬───────┘
140	              ┌─────▼─────┐          ┌──────▼──────┐          ┌──────▼──────┐
141	              │ui/dashboard│         │   ui/nav    │          │ui/song_select│
142	              │ (BASE,lyr0)│         │ (OVR1,lyr1) │          │ (OVR2,lyr2)  │
143	              └────────────┘         └─────────────┘          └──────────────┘
144	   each: owns its widgets + interactions; composition root = its screen OnShow hook
145	```
146	
147	- **`ui_manager`** (promoted from today's `compositor.c`) owns the *mechanism*: string-table
148	  setup, calling `screenInit_/screenShow_`, re-hosting roots onto the right layer, the canvas
149	  buffer pool, layer visibility, and the coexist/replace verbs. It is the "top-level module
150	  that ties everything together."
151	- **Per-screen/overlay modules** own only their panel's content + event wiring, registered
152	  from their own `OnShow` composition root. They never call `legato_*`/canvas APIs directly —
153	  they go through `ui_manager`, which is what keeps the layer mechanics swappable.
154	
155	## 7. Build state & refactor plan

205	Built the operator-UI presentation layer from the GFX Canvas component up to a complete, polished slide-out nav drawer. Arc of the session (decision log has the rationale for each; [`ui_compositor.md`](ui_compositor.md) is the authoritative design):

207	- **Canvas substrate.** Reviewed two MGS canvas regens; adopted GFX Canvas as the surface↔layer substrate. Hit + diagnosed a **silent boot hang** = `heap_1` exhaustion (canvas pushed past 40 KB) firing the IRQ-off malloc-failed hook → raised heap to 65536 and patched both fault hooks to emit a DBGU marker; `APP_Tasks` logs the heap floor.
208	- **State machine off.** Disabled MGS "Generate Screen State Machine" so the app owns `screenInit/Show` and panels coexist live (global layerList; no active-screen gate). Worked around the MGS dangling-`le_gen_init.h` bug with the `compat/` stub (now screen-header-free → immune to screen churn).
209	- **Module split.** `compositor.c` → `ui_manager` (orchestrator) + `ui/nav`. Nav became its own `Navigation` MGS Screen re-hosted onto OVR1 via `leRemoveRootWidget`/`leAddRootWidget` — the "MGS Screen as widget-tree factory" model. Renamed the main screen Marvin → Dashboard, retired `Screen0`. `LE_LAYER_COUNT`=3 pinned by a never-shown `LayerBudget` screen.
210	- **Nav behavior.** Single-active highlight (two schemes; momentary buttons can't hold pressed, confirmed in the widget source), runtime-registered shared release sink, hamburger toggle, Dashboard-closes/others-switch, rounded corners (`cornerRadius`, no AA).
211	- **Slide.** Re-enabled canvas Move FX. Chased two real gotchas to a clean slide: the off-screen window-clip **row-wrap** (clip aligns X down to ×4 and wraps at \|X\|=NAV_W → `NAV_CLOSED_X` stays in-bounds + the layer is disabled on move-done), and the **mid-slide reverse race** (`gfxcStartEffectMove` is a no-op while a move runs → `nav_slide_to` cancels the in-flight move first).

151	     * up by SYS_Initialize (FLEXCOM1_USART_Initialize), so this just arms the
152	     * ring-buffer RX notification and starts the link tasks. */
153	    FretboardLink_Initialize();
154	
155	    /* timing_pipeline runs the chord-window + strum scheduler against the
156	     * active detector and pushes the resulting 7-bit mask through
157	     * FretboardLink_Send. */
158	    TimingPipeline_Initialize();
159	
160	    /* manual_control is a peer producer for direct UI-driven actuation
161	     * (game-menu navigation, manual test). UI buttons are authored in
162	     * Microchip Graphics Composer; the generated screenShow_Screen0
163	     * registers the event_Screen0_Button_Manual_* callbacks defined in
164	     * ui/manual_input.c, so no explicit bind step is needed here. */
165	    ManualControl_Initialize();
166	
167	    /* Game-state observer (spec §4.8, M9): a video-frame consumer that
168	     * classifies the current GH3 screen and publishes game_state_t events on
169	     * xGameStateQueue. Like cv_marvin_v1 it subscribes to the video frame queue
170	     * from inside its task, so it follows Video_Initialize. Enable observation
171	     * explicitly (default off, per the §6 game_observe_enable toggle). */
172	    GameplayEngine_Initialize();
173	    GameplayEngine_SetObserveEnabled(true);
174	
175	    /* SD-card storage: sets up mount state only (no I/O here — the SDMMC
176	     * driver hasn't analyzed the card pre-scheduler). The card is mounted on
177	     * demand by the `sd` console command; see storage/storage.h. */
178	    Storage_Initialize();
179	
180	    /* Per-player results log (CSV on the card). State only here; file I/O is

182	     * console commands. */
183	    Results_Initialize();
184	
185	    /* Song catalog (labels keyed by the recognizer's (setlist,index)). State

188	     * and never affects recognition. See game/catalog.h. */
189	    Catalog_Initialize();
190	
191	    /* Interactive operator console on FLEXCOM2 (115200), separate from the
192	     * DBGU log channel. Started after the actuator/detector modules so its
193	     * commands can drive their setters. */
194	    Console_Initialize();
195	
196	    /* Drain task is launched last so every producer's queue handle is
197	     * already valid when the first records hit the sink. Marvin creates
198	     * all tasks pre-scheduler (Harmony brings the scheduler up after
199	     * APP_Initialize returns); xTaskCreateStatic before vTaskStartScheduler
200	     * is the standard FreeRTOS pattern. */
201	    PerfLog_Start();
202	}

205	/******************************************************************************
206	  Function:
207	    void APP_Tasks ( void )
208	
209	  Remarks:
210	    See prototype in app.h.
211	 */
212	
213	void APP_Tasks ( void )
214	{
215	    /* All tasks have been created by now, so this is the heap_1 startup floor
216	     * (heap_1 never frees — free space only shrinks). Surfaces remaining
217	     * headroom so a future allocation walking into the wall is visible rather
218	     * than a silent malloc-failed spin. */
219	    LOG_INFO("freertos heap: %u bytes free\r\n", (unsigned)xPortGetFreeHeapSize());
220	
221	    /* APP is a one-shot launcher — task creation happened in APP_Initialize.
222	     * Self-delete here so the (1024-word) stack and TCB are released to the
223	     * idle task. The MCC-generated lAPP_Tasks loop will not iterate again
224	     * because vTaskDelete(NULL) never returns to its caller. */
225	    vTaskDelete(NULL);
226	}

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-26 17:04:38Z)**_

This fits the architecture cleanly, and it's actually the perfect vehicle for an open item the compositor doc already flagged. Here's my read before we lock an approach.

## How it maps to what's there

**"Turn on the display" = enable the backlight.** The XLCDC/LVDS panel scans continuously from `SYS_Initialize`; the only real on/off gate is `XLCDC_EnableBacklight()`, currently called unconditionally early in `video_task` ([video.c:313](firmware/marvin/default/src/video/video.c#L313)). So the splash mechanism is: keep the backlight off, get the splash pixels into the BASE framebuffer, *then* enable the backlight — the first lit frame is the splash. (Today there's actually a small window where a half-rendered dashboard can flash at boot; this fixes that too.)

**The splash is just another base view on BASE/layer 0.** BASE is the full-screen Legato canvas (`s_fb_base`, RGB565, in `.region_nocache` — [ui_manager.c:23](firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/ui_manager.c#L23)). Showing splash → later swapping to the dashboard is exactly the **"replace" verb** and the **base-view-replacement open item** in `ui_compositor.md` §10. So this is the first real exercise of that path, not a one-off.

**Runtime JPEG decode is already supported.** `LE_ENABLE_JPEG_DECODER=1`, and `leImage_Create(img, w, h, mode, data, locationID)` builds a runtime `leImage` with `format = LE_IMAGE_FORMAT_JPEG` pointing at a RAM buffer — the decoder runs on draw and converts to the canvas's RGB565. This is the exact path the catalog/album-art plan in the journal assumed ("decoded at startup via Legato's already-enabled decoders, no new library"). Worth treating "decode a 1280×800 SD JPEG to BASE" as the first bring-up gate, since it also de-risks album art.

**Sequencing constraint:** SD mount + FatFs + decode all need the scheduler running (they block on I/O), but `UiManager_Initialize` runs pre-scheduler. So the splash *flow* is a post-scheduler loading task:

```
pre-scheduler:  build Splash + Dashboard + Nav screens; host Splash on BASE (not Dashboard); backlight OFF
loading task:   Storage_Mount → read splash.jpg into staging buf → set image on Splash → leUpdate
                → XLCDC_EnableBacklight()   ← first light = splash
                → [other loading: album-art preload, catalog warm, …]  (progress shown on splash)
                → swap BASE: Splash → Dashboard; Video_CaptureEnable/HEO
```

A few things I'd default unless you object: splash at `/marvin/ui/splash.jpg` with a checked-in seed under `data/ui/` (mirrors the catalog convention); a fixed static staging buffer with a documented size cap (full-screen photo JPEGs run ~0.2–1 MB — I'd cap ~1 MB, 32-byte aligned, skip splash if a file exceeds it); the loading orchestration as a small `screens/splash/` module + a loader, with `ui_manager` owning the BASE swap. Full-screen software JPEG decode on this ARM926 will cost a few hundred ms — fine for a one-time splash.

Two forks are genuinely yours to call:

<tool-use data-tool-type="generic" data-tool-name="AskUserQuestion"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **AskUserQuestion**</summary>
**How should the splash be rendered into the BASE layer?**

Options:
- **MGS Splash screen** - Author a minimal Splash screen in MGS (full-screen image widget + optional 'Loading' / progress label); runtime-set its image to the decoded SD JPEG. Consistent with Dashboard/Nav; progress UI is trivial; clean use of the replace verb. Requires you to author it in Graphics Composer.
- **Code-drawn, no MGS** - Loader decodes + draws the JPEG (and any progress text) straight into the BASE canvas in C — no MGS round-trip. Simpler to land now, but off the screen-as-widget-factory model and progress UI is hand-drawn.
- **Direct HW layer** - Decode into a dedicated framebuffer and point the BASE hardware layer at it directly (bypass Legato), then hand BASE back to the Legato dashboard after. Most timing control, most plumbing, furthest from the compositor model.

**What should happen if the SD card is absent/slow or splash.jpg is missing?**

Options:
- **Skip to dashboard** - Short SD-mount timeout; if no splash, enable backlight showing the dashboard (≈ current boot behavior). Simplest, never blocks boot on a missing card.
- **Solid-color splash** - Always show a clean first frame: a solid brand color (+ 'Loading') drawn into BASE if the JPEG is missing, then proceed to dashboard. No black/garbage ever.
- **Black until ready** - Only ever light the backlight once splash is decoded. Cleanest when SD is healthy, but risks a longer black screen on SD trouble.


**Answer:** I think MGS splash screen, but we'd want full RGB888 for best image quality. will Legato / MGS allow for this without jumping through hoops? In general, graphical display only needs RGB565 once we're past the splash screen., Solid-color splash

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-26 17:11:09Z)**_

The good news: **RGB888 is genuinely clean here — no hoops.** I found the mechanism in [gfx_canvas.c:320](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/gfx/canvas/gfx_canvas.c#L320) — when a canvas is bound to a layer, the framework issues `GFX_IOCTL_SET_LAYER_COLOR_MODE` from `pixelBuffer.mode`, so **the canvas's color mode auto-configures the XLCDC layer**. Color mode is per-canvas via `gfxcSetPixelBuffer(id, w, h, mode, buf)`, the decoder decodes to whatever mode the target canvas is, and `GFX_COLOR_MODE_RGBA_8888` is right there (the canvas component's own default is already 32bpp). So an MGS splash screen rendered into a 32bpp canvas "just works" — no register poking, no MCC/project-wide color-mode change.

That makes your "RGB888 splash, RGB565 everything else" exactly achievable:

## Recommended approach

**BASE canvas (slot 0) is XRGB8888 during the splash, then switched to RGB565 for the dashboard.** The switch is a single `gfxcSetPixelBuffer(0, 1280, 800, GFX_COLOR_MODE_RGB_565, s_fb_base)` at handoff — the framework re-sets the layer mode to 16bpp on the next show. So:

- **Splash** renders into `s_fb_splash` (1280×800×4 = 4.1 MB, 32bpp, `.region_nocache`).
- **Dashboard** keeps `s_fb_base` (1280×800×2 = 2 MB, RGB565) — unchanged from today.
- The splash buffer isn't wasted afterward: it's the natural **decode scratch for album-art preload** (the next loading task). Static-allocation discipline holds and nothing's idle.
- **Canvas count stays 3** — splash reuses the BASE slot (canvas 0), adds no Legato layer, so the `LayerBudget` pin is untouched.

**Boot sequence** (loader runs as a short-lived post-scheduler task, self-deletes after handoff):
```
pre-scheduler:  build Splash + Dashboard + Nav; host SPLASH on BASE (32bpp); backlight OFF
loader task:    Storage_Mount → read /marvin/ui/splash.jpg into staging buf
                → set image on Splash screen → leUpdate (decodes to 32bpp BASE)
                → Video_EnableBacklight()         ← first light = splash
                → album-art preload / catalog warm  (progress on splash)
                → ui_manager swaps BASE: Splash(32bpp) → Dashboard(RGB565); Video capture/HEO on
                → self-delete
```

- **Backlight** moves out of `video_task`'s unconditional init into `Video_EnableBacklight()`, called by the loader (kills the current boot flash too).
- **Solid-color fallback** is free: the MGS Splash screen carries a solid brand-color background, so a missing/oversized JPEG or absent SD just leaves the solid color (+ "Loading"), then proceeds.

**New files:** `screens/splash/screen_splash.{c,h}` (runtime image + progress wiring) and a loader (I'd put the BASE Splash→Dashboard swap in `ui_manager` since the replace verb is its job, and the mount/decode/preload orchestration in a small `ui/loader.c` or `boot.c`). Plus a ~1 MB cached staging buffer for the compressed JPEG (cap it; skip splash if a file exceeds it).

**Your part:** author the Splash screen in Graphics Composer — solid bg fill + a full-screen `leImageWidget` (image set at runtime) + optionally a progress label/bar. I wire decode/sequencing/swap around it.

**First bring-up gate:** decoding a 1280×800 SD JPEG into the 32bpp BASE canvas — proving that also de-risks the whole album-art path.

Two small confirmations before I write this up as a plan:

1. **v1 progress UI** — static splash (just the image + "Loading"), or a real progress bar driven by the loader's stage count? Static is faster to land; the bar is easy to add later.
2. **Asset path / seed** — I'm assuming `/marvin/ui/splash.jpg` with a checked-in seed under `data/ui/splash.jpg` (mirrors the catalog convention). Do you have a splash image, or should I drop in a placeholder seed?

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-26 17:13:44Z)**_

Your timing intuition is right for JPEG — the SD read is tiny (~100–400 KB → ~0.1 s) and the cost is the software decode (a few hundred ms on this ARM926, one-time on the loading task). BMP inverts it: ~3–4 MB read (~0.7 s at our benched read speed) with essentially no decode. Both are sub-second to first light, JPEG usually slightly faster.

But there's a catch that tips it: **BMP isn't a format Legato can decode.** The enabled decoders are RAW, JPEG, PNG — and Legato's "RAW" is its *own* internal pixel-blob layout, not the .bmp file format. So a `.bmp` off the SD card means:
- writing our own BMP parser (header + bottom-up rows + BGR→canvas conversion), and
- blitting raw into the canvas buffer **outside** the `leImageWidget` path — which throws away the MGS-splash-screen approach you picked, and
- it proves nothing reusable, whereas the JPEG path is *exactly* what album-art preload will use.

So I'd stay with **JPEG**: zero custom firmware code, full reuse of the MGS image widget + Legato decoder, and it de-risks album art in the same stroke. At a high JPEG quality the result is visually indistinguishable from uncompressed, decoded straight to 32bpp.

Two refinements worth knowing:
- **If the splash is a logo / flat-color design rather than a photo, use PNG instead** — lossless, compresses far better than BMP, and it's also Legato-decodable (`LE_ENABLE_PNG_DECODER=1`). JPEG if it's photographic.
- **If we ever want "uncompressed, no decode" through the Legato pipeline**, the correct form is a Legato **RAW blob** (an offline tool emits the exact 32bpp layout), *not* BMP — same ~4 MB file but it decodes via the enabled RAW decoder and still works with `leImageWidget`. I'd only reach for that if measured JPEG decode latency actually bothers us on hardware, and since both go through `leImage` it's a trivial swap later.

Net: JPEG (or PNG for a logo) keeps it zero-custom-code and reuse-aligned. Want me to write this up as the plan now — placeholder splash asset, static "Loading" splash, JPEG path, RGB888 splash canvas → RGB565 dashboard swap, backlight gated on splash-ready?

28	/* Scratch for the bench write/read. Static so it stays off the caller's

30	 * fast path: the FatFs diskio bounces a cache-unaligned write buffer through a
31	 * single 512 B sector buffer (~10x slower), while reads stay multi-block even
32	 * when unaligned — which is why an unaligned buffer is write-slow but read-fast.
33	 * Any buffer handed to SYS_FS_FileWrite for throughput wants this alignment. */
34	static uint8_t s_chunk[STG_CHUNK] __ALIGNED(CACHE_LINE_SIZE);

48	/* Throughput in whole MB/s ×10 (one decimal), integer math. */
49	static uint32_t mbps_x10(uint32_t bytes, uint32_t ms)
50	{
51	    if (ms == 0u) { return 0u; }
52	    return (uint32_t)(((uint64_t)bytes * 1000u * 10u) / ((uint64_t)1024u * 1024u * ms));
53	}

55	/* Deterministic pattern as a function of absolute byte offset, so a read can
56	 * verify without retaining what was written. */
57	static void fill_chunk(uint8_t *b, uint32_t chunk_index)
58	{
59	    uint32_t base = chunk_index * STG_CHUNK;
60	    for (uint32_t i = 0u; i < STG_CHUNK; i++)
61	    {
62	        uint32_t off = base + i;
63	        b[i] = (uint8_t)(off ^ (off >> 8));
64	    }
65	}

68	{
69	    uint32_t base = chunk_index * STG_CHUNK;
70	    for (uint32_t i = 0u; i < STG_CHUNK; i++)
71	    {
72	        uint32_t off = base + i;
73	        if (b[i] != (uint8_t)(off ^ (off >> 8))) { return false; }
74	    }
75	    return true;
76	}

124	/* FatFs time hook. Overrides the __WEAK stub in the generated diskio.c (which
125	 * returns a fixed 2013 date) so file timestamps come from the RTC, in UTC.
126	 * FatFs calls this on every create/modify (FF_FS_NORTC=0). The DOS format
127	 * stores year-1980 and seconds/2; FatFs rejects years before 1980, so an
128	 * unset/implausible RTC falls back to the 1980 epoch. */
129	DWORD get_fattime(void)
130	{
131	    struct tm now;
132	    memset(&now, 0, sizeof(now));
133	    RTC_TimeGet(&now);
134	
135	    SYS_FS_TIME t;
136	    t.packedTime = 0u;
137	
138	    int year = now.tm_year + 1900;
139	    if (year < 1980)
140	    {
141	        t.discreteTime.year  = 0u;   /* 1980 */
142	        t.discreteTime.month = 1u;
143	        t.discreteTime.day   = 1u;
144	        return t.packedTime;
145	    }
146	
147	    t.discreteTime.year   = (unsigned)(year - 1980);
148	    t.discreteTime.month  = (unsigned)(now.tm_mon + 1);
149	    t.discreteTime.day    = (unsigned)now.tm_mday;
150	    t.discreteTime.hour   = (unsigned)now.tm_hour;
151	    t.discreteTime.minute = (unsigned)now.tm_min;
152	    t.discreteTime.second = (unsigned)(now.tm_sec / 2);   /* DOS stores sec/2 */
153	    return t.packedTime;
154	}

225	void Storage_DiagBench(storage_print_fn out, void *ctx, uint32_t mbytes)
226	{

228	    {
229	        diag_printf(out, ctx, "not mounted");
230	        return;
231	    }
232	
233	    if (mbytes == 0u)               { mbytes = 4u; }
234	    if (mbytes > STG_BENCH_MAX_MB)  { mbytes = STG_BENCH_MAX_MB; }
235	
236	    uint32_t chunks      = (mbytes * 1024u * 1024u) / STG_CHUNK;
237	    uint32_t total_bytes = chunks * STG_CHUNK;
238	
239	    /* write */
240	    SYS_FS_HANDLE h = SYS_FS_FileOpen(STG_TESTFILE, SYS_FS_FILE_OPEN_WRITE);
241	    if (h == SYS_FS_HANDLE_INVALID)
242	    {
243	        diag_printf(out, ctx, "open(write) failed (fs err %d)", (int)SYS_FS_Error());
244	        return;
245	    }
246	    TickType_t t0 = xTaskGetTickCount();
247	    bool write_err = false;
248	    for (uint32_t c = 0u; c < chunks; c++)
249	    {
250	        fill_chunk(s_chunk, c);
251	        if (SYS_FS_FileWrite(h, s_chunk, STG_CHUNK) != STG_CHUNK)
252	        {
253	            write_err = true;
254	            break;
255	        }
256	    }

258	    uint32_t wms = (uint32_t)((xTaskGetTickCount() - t0) * portTICK_PERIOD_MS);
259	    if (write_err)

261	        diag_printf(out, ctx, "write failed (fs err %d)", (int)SYS_FS_Error());
262	        return;
263	    }

265	                (unsigned long)(total_bytes / 1024u), (unsigned long)wms,
266	                (unsigned long)(mbps_x10(total_bytes, wms) / 10u),
267	                (unsigned long)(mbps_x10(total_bytes, wms) % 10u));
268	
269	    /* read back + verify */

271	    if (h == SYS_FS_HANDLE_INVALID)
272	    {
273	        diag_printf(out, ctx, "open(read) failed (fs err %d)", (int)SYS_FS_Error());
274	        return;
275	    }
276	    TickType_t r0 = xTaskGetTickCount();
277	    bool read_err = false, mismatch = false;
278	    for (uint32_t c = 0u; c < chunks; c++)
279	    {

281	        {

#ifndef UI_SCREEN_SPLASH_H
#define UI_SCREEN_SPLASH_H

#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdint.h>

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/* Boot splash — a full-screen image shown on BASE while the loader mounts the
 * SD card and pre-loads assets, then replaced by the Dashboard (ui_manager's
 * "replace" verb). Authored in code (one image widget over a solid-fill root),
 * not MGS: the tree is trivial and this keeps the splash self-contained and
 * testable without an MGS round-trip. Hosted on BASE by ui_manager; the BASE
 * canvas is 32bpp (XRGB8888) for the splash's lifetime so the photo keeps full
 * color depth, then ui_manager switches BASE back to RGB565 for the dashboard.
 *
 * If no image is set (missing/oversized splash.jpg, no card) the root's solid
 * fill is the fallback "splash" — a clean first frame either way. */

#define SPLASH_W   1280u
#define SPLASH_H    800u

/* Build the splash widget tree. Call once, before the scheduler (peer to the
 * screenInit_ calls in ui_manager). */
void Splash_Init(void);

/* The splash root, for ui_manager to attach to / detach from the BASE layer. */
struct leWidget;
struct leWidget *Splash_Root(void);

/* Point the splash image widget at a JPEG held in memory (the loader's staging
 * buffer, read from SD). `data` must stay valid while the splash is shown — the
 * decoder reads it on each paint. Dimensions are assumed SPLASH_W x SPLASH_H.
 * Returns false if data is NULL/len is 0 (caller shows the solid-fill fallback). */
bool Splash_SetImageJpeg(void *data, uint32_t len);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif /* UI_SCREEN_SPLASH_H */

#include "ui/screens/splash/screen_splash.h"

#include <stddef.h>

#include "gfx/legato/legato.h"
#include "gfx/legato/widget/legato_widget.h"
#include "gfx/legato/widget/image/legato_widget_image.h"
#include "gfx/legato/image/legato_image.h"
#include "gfx/legato/generated/le_gen_scheme.h"

/* Built once in Splash_Init, attached to BASE by ui_manager. Allocated from the
 * Legato widget pool (LE_MALLOC) like every MGS widget; never freed (one-shot,
 * and heap_1 never frees) — ui_manager detaches the root at the dashboard swap. */
static leWidget      *s_root;
static leImageWidget *s_image;

/* Runtime image descriptor pointing at the loader's in-memory JPEG. Layout
 * mirrors a generated leImage (see le_gen_images.c): the stream descriptor and
 * the pixel buffer both carry the compressed byte length; pixel_count is the
 * decoded pixel count; buffer.mode is the decode output mode (888 for full
 * color — the BASE canvas is 32bpp and converts on blit). */
static leImage        s_img;

void Splash_Init(void)
{
    s_root = leWidget_New();
    s_root->fn->setPosition(s_root, 0, 0);
    s_root->fn->setSize(s_root, SPLASH_W, SPLASH_H);
    s_root->fn->setScheme(s_root, &SCHEME_BACKGROUND);
    s_root->fn->setBackgroundType(s_root, LE_WIDGET_BACKGROUND_FILL);
    s_root->fn->setMargins(s_root, 0, 0, 0, 0);

    s_image = leImageWidget_New();
    s_image->fn->setPosition(s_image, 0, 0);
    s_image->fn->setSize(s_image, SPLASH_W, SPLASH_H);
    s_image->fn->setBackgroundType(s_image, LE_WIDGET_BACKGROUND_NONE);
    s_root->fn->addChild(s_root, (leWidget *)s_image);
}

leWidget *Splash_Root(void)
{
    return s_root;
}

bool Splash_SetImageJpeg(void *data, uint32_t len)
{
    if (data == NULL || len == 0u || s_image == NULL) { return false; }

    s_img = (leImage){
        {                                       /* leStreamDescriptor header */
            LE_STREAM_LOCATION_ID_INTERNAL,     /* data is in MCU memory      */
            data,
            len,
        },
        LE_IMAGE_FORMAT_JPEG,
        {                                       /* lePixelBuffer buffer       */
            LE_COLOR_MODE_RGB_888,
            { (int32_t)SPLASH_W, (int32_t)SPLASH_H },
            SPLASH_W * SPLASH_H,                /* pixel_count (decoded)      */
            len,                                /* buffer_length (compressed) */
            data,
            0,
        },
        0,                                      /* image flags */
        { 0 },                                  /* mask (color) */
        NULL,                                   /* alpha mask   */
        NULL,                                   /* palette      */
    };

    return s_image->fn->setImage(s_image, &s_img) == LE_SUCCESS;
}

```

#ifndef UI_LOADER_H
#define UI_LOADER_H

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/* Boot loader — a one-shot task that runs the startup sequence the splash
 * fronts: mount the SD card, read the splash image onto the (already-shown)
 * splash screen, light the backlight, run asset pre-load (album art, …), then
 * hand BASE from the splash to the dashboard and bring the camera up. Create
 * from APP_Initialize (pre-scheduler); the task self-deletes after the handoff.
 *
 * Why a task and not APP_Initialize: SD mount + FatFs + JPEG decode all block
 * on I/O and need the scheduler running, whereas APP_Initialize runs before it. */
void Loader_Start(void);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif /* UI_LOADER_H */

```c
#include "ui/loader.h"

#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>

#include "FreeRTOS.h"
#include "task.h"

#include "definitions.h"
#include "log.h"
#include "storage/storage.h"
#include "video/video.h"
#include "ui/ui_manager.h"
#include "ui/screens/splash/screen_splash.h"

#define LOADER_TASK_STACK_WORDS  1024u
#define LOADER_TASK_PRIORITY     2u    /* UI band; yields on SD I/O + delays */

#define SPLASH_REL_PATH    "/ui/splash.jpg"
#define SPLASH_JPEG_MAX    (1024u * 1024u)   /* cap; skip splash if file is larger */
#define SPLASH_READ_CHUNK  (64u * 1024u)

/* Time for the splash image to decode + composite before we light the panel.
 * The JPEG decode runs inside a Legato paint on LEGATO_Tasks, which we can't
 * cleanly join from here, so this fixed settle covers it (a full-screen
 * software decode is a few hundred ms on this ARM926). Tune on hardware —
 * replace with a real paint-complete signal if the photo ever lights mid-decode. */
#define SPLASH_RENDER_SETTLE_MS  500u
#define SPLASH_BG_SETTLE_MS       80u   /* solid-fill fallback: just one composite */
#define SPLASH_MIN_MS           1200u   /* hold the splash at least this long */

/* Video window: 720×480 video at (280, 76) on the 1280×800 panel — 1:1 with the
 * bridge's typical 480p source, leaving a UI strip below. */
#define VIDEO_WIN_X   280u
#define VIDEO_WIN_Y    76u
#define VIDEO_WIN_W   720u
#define VIDEO_WIN_H   480u

/* Compressed splash JPEG, read from SD. Static (off-stack); the leImage handed
 * to Legato points straight at it, so it must stay resident while the splash is
 * shown. Cache-line aligned for the FatFs multi-block read fast path. */
static uint8_t s_jpeg[SPLASH_JPEG_MAX] __ALIGNED(CACHE_LINE_SIZE);

static StackType_t  s_task_stack[LOADER_TASK_STACK_WORDS];
static StaticTask_t s_task_tcb;

/* Read the splash file into s_jpeg. Returns byte count, or 0 on any failure
 * (no card, missing file, too large, short read) — caller falls back to the
 * splash's solid fill. */
static uint32_t load_splash_file(void)
{
    if (!Storage_Mount()) { return 0u; }

    char path[64];
    (void)snprintf(path, sizeof(path), "%s%s", Storage_MountPoint(), SPLASH_REL_PATH);

    SYS_FS_HANDLE h = SYS_FS_FileOpen(path, SYS_FS_FILE_OPEN_READ);
    if (h == SYS_FS_HANDLE_INVALID)
    {
        LOG_WARN("LOADER: no splash %s (fs err %d)\r\n", path, (int)SYS_FS_Error());
        return 0u;
    }

    int32_t sz = SYS_FS_FileSize(h);
    if (sz <= 0 || (uint32_t)sz > SPLASH_JPEG_MAX)
    {
        LOG_WARN("LOADER: splash size %ld invalid (cap %u)\r\n",
                 (long)sz, (unsigned)SPLASH_JPEG_MAX);
        (void)SYS_FS_FileClose(h);
        return 0u;
    }

    uint32_t total = 0u;
    bool err = false;
    while (total < (uint32_t)sz)
    {
        size_t want = (size_t)((uint32_t)sz - total);
        if (want > SPLASH_READ_CHUNK) { want = SPLASH_READ_CHUNK; }

        size_t got = SYS_FS_FileRead(h, &s_jpeg[total], want);
        if (got == 0u || got == (size_t)-1) { err = true; break; }
        total += (uint32_t)got;
    }
    (void)SYS_FS_FileClose(h);

    if (err || total != (uint32_t)sz)
    {
        LOG_WARN("LOADER: splash read short %lu/%ld\r\n", (unsigned long)total, (long)sz);
        return 0u;
    }
    LOG_INFO("LOADER: splash %lu B loaded\r\n", (unsigned long)total);
    return total;
}

static void loader_task(void *param)
{
    (void)param;

    uint32_t len = load_splash_file();
    bool have_image = (len > 0u) && Splash_SetImageJpeg(s_jpeg, len);
    if (!have_image) { LOG_WARN("LOADER: solid-fill splash (no image)\r\n"); }

    /* Let the splash composite before lighting the panel: the decoded photo if
     * we have one, else just the solid-fill fallback. */
    vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(have_image ? SPLASH_RENDER_SETTLE_MS : SPLASH_BG_SETTLE_MS));
    Video_EnableBacklight();
    TickType_t shown_at = xTaskGetTickCount();

    /* --- Asset pre-load goes here (album art → DDR cache, etc.). The 32bpp
     * splash buffer (ui_manager) is free to reuse as decode scratch once the
     * splash leaves the screen. None yet. --- */

    /* Hold the splash a minimum time so a fast boot doesn't flash it away. */
    TickType_t elapsed   = xTaskGetTickCount() - shown_at;
    TickType_t min_ticks = pdMS_TO_TICKS(SPLASH_MIN_MS);
    if (elapsed < min_ticks) { vTaskDelay(min_ticks - elapsed); }

    /* Replace the splash with the live UI, then bring the camera up. */
    UiManager_ShowDashboard();
    Video_SetWindow(VIDEO_WIN_X, VIDEO_WIN_Y, VIDEO_WIN_W, VIDEO_WIN_H);
    Video_CaptureEnable();
    Video_DisplayShow();

    vTaskDelete(NULL);
}

void Loader_Start(void)
{
    (void)xTaskCreateStatic(loader_task, "LoaderTask", LOADER_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
                            NULL, LOADER_TASK_PRIORITY, s_task_stack, &s_task_tcb);
}

```

import struct, sys, math
W,H = 1280,800
out = sys.argv[1]
# 24bpp BMP, bottom-up, BGR. row stride 1280*3=3840 (4-aligned, no pad).
rows=[]
for y in range(H):
    row=bytearray()
    for x in range(W):
        # photo-ish diagonal gradient + soft vignette so it's clearly an image, not flat
        r=int(40+120*(x/W))
        g=int(30+90*(y/H))
        b=int(90+120*(1-(x/W))*(1-(y/H)))
        v=1-0.5*((( (x-W/2)/W)**2+((y-H/2)/H)**2))
        r=max(0,min(255,int(r*v))); g=max(0,min(255,int(g*v))); b=max(0,min(255,int(b*v)))
        row += bytes((b,g,r))
    rows.append(bytes(row))
pixels=b''.join(reversed(rows))  # bottom-up
stride=W*3
imgsize=stride*H
off=54
bmp=b'BM'+struct.pack('<IHHI',off+imgsize,0,0,off)
bmp+=struct.pack('<IiiHHIIiiII',40,W,H,1,24,0,imgsize,2835,2835,0,0)
open(out,'wb').write(bmp+pixels)
print("wrote",out,off+imgsize,"bytes")
PY

        r=int(40+120*(x/W)); g=int(30+90*(y/H)); b=int(90+120*(1-(x/W))*(1-(y/H)))
        v=1-0.5*((((x-W/2)/W)**2+((y-H/2)/H)**2))
        r=max(0,min(255,int(r*v))); g=max(0,min(255,int(g*v))); b=max(0,min(255,int(b*v)))
        row += bytes((b,g,r))
    rows.append(bytes(row))
pixels=b''.join(reversed(rows)); stride=W*3; imgsize=stride*H; off=54
bmp=b'BM'+struct.pack('<IHHI',off+imgsize,0,0,off)+struct.pack('<IiiHHIIiiII',40,W,H,1,24,0,imgsize,2835,2835,0,0)
open(out,'wb').write(bmp+pixels); print("bmp",off+imgsize)
PY
sips -s format jpeg -s formatOptions 82 "$B" --out data/ui/splash.jpg 2>&1 | tail -2
rm -f "$B"
echo "---"; ls -l data/ui/splash.jpg && file data/ui/splash.jpg
```

203	## 9. Memory budget
204	
205	`.region_nocache` is 32 MB, shared with the ISC capture pool (~10.5 MB) + Legato scratch
206	(0.5 MB). Full-screen RGB565 surface ≈ 2.0 MB; overlays sized to content are far less (nav
207	~320×800 ≈ 0.5 MB; a modal dialog smaller still). ~19 MB free after BASE + capture + scratch,
208	so **memory is not the binding constraint — the 3 UI layers are.**
209	
210	## 10. Open items
211	
212	- **Base-view replacement** detail when a 2nd full-screen view arrives (rebuild vs parked
213	  last-frame on return; how nav persistence interacts with `screenShow`/`Hide` of layer 0).
214	- **`manual_input.c` fate** — `Screen0` retired; the strum handlers now serve the Dashboard
215	  screen, so it stays until manual control is reworked.
216	- **Per-pixel alpha** — which (if any) overlay needs ARGB8888 over the camera vs. layer alpha.
217	
218	## 10a. Anti-aliased rounded button corners (done)
219	
220	The nav buttons use the widget `cornerRadius` (set in code — not exposed in MGS), but the
221	classic skin's rounded-rect fill draws corners with `leRenderer_ArcFill` (hard, stepped
222	edges). Smoothing is done **without touching Legato/MCC code** (`config/default/` is
223	off-limits), via a per-instance vtable re-point in `src/ui/widgets/button_aa/widget_button_aa.c`:
224	
225	- `leWidget.fn` is a writable per-instance pointer to a `const` vtable. `ButtonAA_Enable`
226	  makes one shared writable copy of the button vtable, overrides only `_paint`, and points
227	  the button's `fn`/`widget.fn` at it. No `LE_DYNAMIC_VTABLES` (not an MCC knob; unguarded
228	  `#define 0` in generated `legato_config.h`), no global RAM cost — scoped to re-pointed
229	  buttons.
230	- The wrapper runs the original paint (bg + label + border), then on `DONE` with the
231	  supported radius overdraws the four corners: sample the backdrop from each corner's
232	  extreme pixel (left untouched by the rounded fill), then blend a 1px transition band from
233	  a precomputed coverage mask via `leColorLerp` + `leRenderer_PutPixel`. Fill is read from
234	  the live scheme each paint, so highlight (selected/unselected) and pressed states track.
235	- Runs **in-pass** (damage → repaint → AA in one paint), so no timing/flicker window.
236	- Wired from `nav_buttons_init()`; currently nav-only. Extending app-wide is just calling
237	  `ButtonAA_Enable` from other screens' button init. Single radius (`BUTTON_AA_RADIUS`);
238	  other radii pass through unsmoothed.
239	
240	## 11. Relationship to spec §4.5 / Q5
241	
242	This answers spec **Q5** (Legato vs. custom UI) for the *presentation* layer: **Legato is the
