Good catch — let me answer directly, because you've basically already spotted it.

I looked at what the MGS `Splash` screen actually contains: just `root0` + `Splash_Panel_0` — an empty 1280×800 panel with `SCHEME_BACKGROUND`. No image widget, no text. So it's a bare shell.

**My take: there's little value in the MGS Splash screen for this use case.** Reasoning:

- The only meaningful widget is the photo, and it **can't** be an MGS asset — it's loaded from the SD card at runtime, so it has to be placed/assigned in code no matter what. MGS can't author the thing that matters here.
- The one thing MGS authoring would buy you is laying out *static chrome* visually (logo placement, version string, a progress bar). You said static splash, no progress — so there's nothing to lay out.
- A code-built splash is one self-contained file, no MGS round-trip, and matches the `song_list` precedent for hand-built UI in this repo.
- Using the MGS shell would split the splash across MGS (empty panel) + code (the image) for no real gain, and leaves a near-empty screen to maintain/regenerate in the project.

The *only* reason I'd keep it: if you want every base view to be a uniform MGS screen (`screenInit_/screenShow_/screenHide_`) on principle, for symmetry with Dashboard/Nav. If that matters to you, I'll switch `ui_manager` to call `screenInit_Splash`/`screenShow_Splash` and have `screen_splash.c` add the `leImageWidget` onto `Splash_Panel_0` — same result, just more wiring.

One housekeeping note: `le_gen_screen_Splash.c` is generated and currently staged, so it'll compile as dead code if we don't use it. So we should pick one:

- **Drop it (my recommendation):** you remove the `Splash` screen from the Graphics Composer project so it stops regenerating; I unstage/remove the two generated files. Keep my self-contained `screens/splash/screen_splash.c`.
- **Use it as the shell:** I rewire to `screenShow_Splash` + add the image widget onto `Splash_Panel_0` in code; you keep the screen in MGS.

Want me to go with dropping it? If so, I'll remove the staged generated files (you'll just need to delete the Splash screen in Composer at some point so a regen doesn't bring it back). My current code + docs already assume the code-built approach, so nothing else changes.

```h
/* Boot splash image, layered onto the MGS `Splash` screen.
 *
 * The Splash screen itself (root + full-screen Splash_Panel_0 with a solid
 * scheme fill) is authored in MGS like every base view (le_gen_screen_Splash.c)
 * — kept for the "every base view has an MGS component" convention even though
 * the splash's only real content is loaded, not authored. The photo can't be an
 * MGS asset (it's read off the SD card at runtime), so this module adds one
 * leImageWidget onto the MGS panel in code and points it at the in-memory JPEG.
 * With no image set (missing/oversized splash.jpg, no card) the panel's solid
 * fill is the fallback splash.
 *
 * Order: ui_manager calls screenShow_Splash() (builds the MGS tree) then
 * Splash_AttachImage() (adds the image widget); the loader later calls
 * Splash_SetImageJpeg() once the file is read. */

#define SPLASH_W   1280u
#define SPLASH_H    800u

/* Add the image widget onto the (already-shown) MGS Splash panel. Call once,
 * after screenShow_Splash(), before the first leUpdate. */
void Splash_AttachImage(void);

/* Point the splash image at a JPEG held in memory (the loader's staging
 * buffer). `data` must stay valid while the splash is shown — the decoder reads
 * it on each paint. Assumed SPLASH_W x SPLASH_H. Returns false on bad args or
 * if the image widget isn't attached (caller shows the solid-fill fallback). */
bool Splash_SetImageJpeg(void *data, uint32_t len);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif /* UI_SCREEN_SPLASH_H */
```

```c
#include "ui/screens/splash/screen_splash.h"

#include <stddef.h>

#include "gfx/legato/legato.h"
#include "gfx/legato/widget/legato_widget.h"
#include "gfx/legato/widget/image/legato_widget_image.h"
#include "gfx/legato/image/legato_image.h"
#include "gfx/legato/generated/screen/le_gen_screen_Splash.h"   /* Splash_Panel_0 */

/* The image widget we add onto the MGS Splash panel. Allocated from the Legato
 * widget pool; freed with the rest of the Splash tree by screenHide_Splash
 * (leWidget_Delete) at the dashboard swap, so it must not be touched after. */
static leImageWidget *s_image;

/* Runtime image descriptor pointing at the loader's in-memory JPEG. Layout
 * mirrors a generated leImage (see le_gen_images.c): the stream descriptor and
 * the pixel buffer both carry the compressed byte length; pixel_count is the
 * decoded pixel count; buffer.mode is the decode output mode (888 for full
 * color — the BASE canvas is 32bpp for the splash and converts on blit). */
static leImage        s_img;

void Splash_AttachImage(void)
{
    if (Splash_Panel_0 == NULL) { return; }   /* screenShow_Splash not called */

    s_image = leImageWidget_New();
    s_image->fn->setPosition(s_image, 0, 0);
    s_image->fn->setSize(s_image, SPLASH_W, SPLASH_H);
    s_image->fn->setBackgroundType(s_image, LE_WIDGET_BACKGROUND_NONE);
    Splash_Panel_0->fn->addChild(Splash_Panel_0, (leWidget *)s_image);
}

bool Splash_SetImageJpeg(void *data, uint32_t len)
{
    if (data == NULL || len == 0u || s_image == NULL) { return false; }

    s_img = (leImage){
        {                                       /* leStreamDescriptor header */
            LE_STREAM_LOCATION_ID_INTERNAL,     /* data is in MCU memory      */
            data,
            len,
        },
        LE_IMAGE_FORMAT_JPEG,
        {                                       /* lePixelBuffer buffer       */
            LE_COLOR_MODE_RGB_888,
            { (int32_t)SPLASH_W, (int32_t)SPLASH_H },
            SPLASH_W * SPLASH_H,                /* pixel_count (decoded)      */
            len,                                /* buffer_length (compressed) */
            data,
            0,
        },
        0,                                      /* image flags */
        { 0 },                                  /* mask (color) */
        NULL,                                   /* alpha mask   */
        NULL,                                   /* palette      */
    };

    return s_image->fn->setImage(s_image, &s_img) == LE_SUCCESS;
}
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-26 17:44:35Z)**_

**RGBA8888.** Reasons:

- It matches what the code already uses: `s_fb_splash` is `uint32_t[1280*800]` (4 bytes/pixel) and I set the canvas to `GFX_COLOR_MODE_RGBA_8888`. RGB888 is 24bpp *packed* (3 bytes/pixel), which would force a non-`uint32_t` buffer layout and byte-misaligned pixels — slower for CPU render, and it only saves ~1 MB we don't need.
- It matches the rest of the pipeline (capture is BGRX32, HEO is 32bpp), so BASE at 32bpp is symmetric.
- On BASE (the bottom layer) the alpha byte is ignored, so RGBA8888 is effectively XRGB8888 — you get full RGB888 color quality, just word-aligned. No quality loss vs 24bpp.

Bonus: if you set the **Splash screen's** layer to RGBA8888 in Graphics Composer, `screenShow_Splash` will emit `leSetLayerColorMode(0, RGBA_8888)` itself — and then I can **delete the override** I added in `ui_manager` (the `leSetLayerColorMode(CANVAS_BASE, RGBA_8888)` line after the show). The Dashboard screen stays RGB565, so the two per-screen modes line up with their buffers automatically. Cleaner all around.

So: set Splash → **RGBA8888** in MGS and regen. Once you do, tell me and I'll strip the override (and the redundant 565 re-set at the swap) so `ui_manager` just relies on each MGS screen asserting its own mode. Want me to leave the override in for now (works either way) until you regen?

```text
36:| 2026-06-26 | **Boot splash = full-screen SD JPEG shown on BASE before the backlight comes on; first real use of the compositor "replace" verb. Design in [`ui_compositor.md`](ui_compositor.md) §12. | "Turn on the display" = enable the backlight (XLCDC scans continuously from `SYS_Initialize`), so gating the backlight on splash-ready is the whole mechanism — and it removes the existing boot flash of a half-rendered dashboard. JPEG over BMP/RAW: BMP isn't Legato-decodable (only RAW/JPEG/PNG), so it would mean a custom parser + bypassing the `leImageWidget` path and would prove nothing reusable; JPEG reuses Legato's enabled decoder and **is** the album-art pre-load path. RGB888-without-hoops confirmed in `gfx_canvas.c` (per-canvas mode auto-configures the XLCDC layer), so the splash gets full color depth while the steady-state dashboard stays RGB565 to save DDR bandwidth; the 32bpp splash buffer doubles as future album-art decode scratch. Splash kept as an MGS shell (Greg's call) for base-view uniformity even though its only real content is the loaded image; the image widget is code-added since it's runtime data. Loader is a task (not `APP_Initialize`) because SD mount + FatFs + decode block on I/O and need the scheduler. Known one-time-boot roughness (hard splash→dashboard cut; fixed backlight settle vs a real paint-complete signal; the RGB565→8888 layer-mode override; baseline-JPEG-only) tracked in §10/§12. | 
37:| 2026-06-26 | **Anti-aliased rounded button corners via a per-instance vtable re-point — no Legato/MCC edits (`ui/button_aa.c`).** The classic skin draws rounded corners with `leRenderer_ArcFill` (hard stepped edges). `ButtonAA_Enable(btn)` makes one shared writable copy of the button vtable, overrides only `_paint`, and points the button's `fn`/`widget.fn` at the copy; the wrapper runs the original paint then, on `DONE` at the supported radius, overdraws the four corners — sampling each corner's extreme (untouched) pixel as backdrop and blending a 1px band from a precomputed coverage mask (`leColorLerp` + `leRenderer_PutPixel`). Wired from `nav_buttons_init()` (nav-only for now; extend by adding call sites). Also added a CLAUDE.md rule: do not modify MCC-generated/Legato code under `config/default/`. Design in [`ui_compositor.md`](ui_compositor.md) §10a. | Editing the skin (the obvious spot) is forbidden — it's vendor/MCC code that regen silently overwrites. `LE_DYNAMIC_VTABLES` (the sanctioned global override) is **not** an MCC knob and is an unguarded `#define 0` in generated `legato_config.h` (can't flip via config, can't `-D`, can't hand-edit) — dead end. A post-render overdraw on the nav canvas has no vendor-legal post-paint hook and fights Legato's damage-repaint (1-frame hard-corner flash). The per-instance re-point exploits that `leWidget.fn` is a *writable* pointer to a const vtable: it needs no config flag, costs one vtable struct + one mask in BSS (static-allocation discipline holds), runs **in-pass** (repaint→AA same paint, no timing window), and is scoped to exactly the buttons we re-point. **Confirmed on hardware** — smooth corners across selected/unselected/pressed states and slide cycles. |
47:| 2026-06-23 | **RTC enabled in Gregorian mode, kept in UTC; FatFs file timestamps wired to it.** Added the SAM9X75 internal RTC via MCC (Gregorian/`struct tm` plib `RTC_TimeSet/Get`, `RTC_Initialize` in `SYS_Initialize`); `RTC_MR.UTC=0` (calendar register format) but the clock *value* is set in UTC. Console gains `time` / `time set YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` (prints ISO-8601 `…Z`, computes weekday). A strong `get_fattime()` in `storage.c` overrides the generated `__WEAK` stub (which hardcoded 2013-08-09) so files carry RTC time (year-1980, sec/2 DOS packing; <1980 falls back to the epoch). Resolves the timestamp half of Q12. **No backup cell populated yet** → RTC resets on power-off and must be re-set at boot (host via `time set`); persistent wall-clock needs VDDBU backup hardware. | "UTC mode" (the `RTC_MR.UTC` seconds-counter format) vs Gregorian is orthogonal to keeping a UTC *value* — Gregorian was chosen because FatFs `get_fattime` (mandatory, `FF_FS_NORTC=0`) wants broken-down fields, so calendar registers feed it directly with no epoch conversion, while a UTC value gives DST/timezone-proof timestamps matching the spec's `session_started_utc` `…Z` convention (§4.6.5). `get_fattime` as a `__WEAK` override keeps it out of the regenerated diskio.c. Keeping CSI/ISC/CSI2DC peripheral/driver layers — we'll drive those directly from the TC358743 module. Greg regenerating MCC. |

438:- **Boot order (SAM9X75 ROM, from the Microchip boot-process page):** sequential fall-through **SDMMC0 → SDMMC1 → QSPI → NAND → SPI(FLEXCOM5)**, first valid image wins, customizable only via the OTP Boot Configuration Packet. So SD outranks NAND (good for an SD override/recovery with NAND resident), and **QSPI must be empty/disabled for NAND to boot** (it's checked first). The JTAG dev loop pulls JP3+JP4 and uses no card → ROM falls through to the SAM-BA monitor.

Canvas count stays 3 (splash reuses the BASE slot). Missing/oversized/no-card → the panel's solid fill is the fallback. Seed `data/ui/splash.jpg` (placeholder). Design in [`ui_compositor.md`](ui_compositor.md) §12. | "Turn on the display" = enable the backlight (XLCDC scans continuously from `SYS_Initialize`), so gating the backlight on splash-ready is the whole mechanism — and it removes the existing boot flash of a half-rendered dashboard. JPEG over BMP/RAW: BMP isn't Legato-decodable (only RAW/JPEG/PNG), so it would mean a custom parser + bypassing the `leImageWidget` path and would prove nothing reusable; JPEG reuses Legato's enabled decoder and **is** the album-art pre-load path. RGB888-without-hoops confirmed in `gfx_canvas.c` (per-canvas mode auto-configures the XLCDC layer), so the splash gets full color depth while the steady-state dashboard stays RGB565 to save DDR bandwidth; the 32bpp splash buffer doubles as future album-art decode scratch. Splash kept as an MGS shell (Greg's call) for base-view uniformity even though its only real content is the loaded image; the image widget is code-added since it's runtime data. Loader is a task (not `APP_Initialize`) because SD mount + FatFs + decode block on I/O and need the scheduler. Known one-time-boot roughness (hard splash→dashboard cut; fixed backlight settle vs a real paint-complete signal; the RGB565→8888 layer-mode override; baseline-JPEG-only) tracked in §10/§12. | 
37:| 2026-06-26 | **Anti-aliased rounded button corners via a per-instance vtable re-point — no Legato/MCC edits (`ui/button_aa.c`).** The classic skin draws rounded corners with `leRenderer_ArcFill` (hard stepped edges). `ButtonAA_Enable(btn)` makes one shared writable copy of the button vtable, overrides only `_paint`, and points the button's `fn`/`widget.fn` at the copy; the wrapper runs the original paint then, on `DONE` at the supported radius, overdraws the four corners — sampling each corner's extreme (untouched) pixel as backdrop and blending a 1px band from a precomputed coverage mask (`leColorLerp` + `leRenderer_PutPixel`). Wired from `nav_buttons_init()` (nav-only for now; extend by adding call sites). Also added a CLAUDE.md rule: do not modify MCC-generated/Legato code under `config/default/`. Design in [`ui_compositor.md`](ui_compositor.md) §10a. | Editing the skin (the obvious spot) is forbidden — it's vendor/MCC code that regen silently overwrites. `LE_DYNAMIC_VTABLES` (the sanctioned global override) is **not** an MCC knob and is an unguarded `#define 0` in generated `legato_config.h` (can't flip via config, can't `-D`, can't hand-edit) — dead end. A post-render overdraw on the nav canvas has no vendor-legal post-paint hook and fights Legato's damage-repaint (1-frame hard-corner flash). The per-instance re-point exploits that `leWidget.fn` is a *writable* pointer to a const vtable: it needs no config flag, costs one vtable struct + one mask in BSS (static-allocation discipline holds), runs **in-pass** (repaint→AA same paint, no timing window), and is scoped to exactly the buttons we re-point. **Confirmed on hardware** — smooth corners across selected/unselected/pressed states and slide cycles. |
47:| 2026-06-23 | **RTC enabled in Gregorian mode, kept in UTC; FatFs file timestamps wired to it.** Added the SAM9X75 internal RTC via MCC (Gregorian/`struct tm` plib `RTC_TimeSet/Get`, `RTC_Initialize` in `SYS_Initialize`); `RTC_MR.UTC=0` (calendar register format) but the clock *value* is set in UTC. Console gains `time` / `time set YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` (prints ISO-8601 `…Z`, computes weekday). A strong `get_fattime()` in `storage.c` overrides the generated `__WEAK` stub (which hardcoded 2013-08-09) so files carry RTC time (year-1980, sec/2 DOS packing; <1980 falls back to the epoch). Resolves the timestamp half of Q12. **No backup cell populated yet** → RTC resets on power-off and must be re-set at boot (host via `time set`); persistent wall-clock needs VDDBU backup hardware. | "UTC mode" (the `RTC_MR.UTC` seconds-counter format) vs Gregorian is orthogonal to keeping a UTC *value* — Gregorian was chosen because FatFs `get_fattime` (mandatory, `FF_FS_NORTC=0`) wants broken-down fields, so calendar registers feed it directly with no epoch conversion, while a UTC value gives DST/timezone-proof timestamps matching the spec's `session_started_utc` `…Z` convention (§4.6.5). `get_fattime` as a `__WEAK` override keeps it out of the regenerated diskio.c. Player identity + whether to add VDDBU backup remain open under Q12. |
```

## Final state — boot splash (code-complete, pending your MPLAB build + hardware test)

**Flow:** panel stays dark → loader mounts SD, reads `/<card>/ui/splash.jpg` into a static buffer, sets it on the splash image widget → backlight on (first light = splash) → [asset preload hook] → min-hold → swap BASE splash→dashboard → camera/HEO go live.

**Files**
- **`screens/splash/screen_splash.{c,h}`** — adds one full-screen `leImageWidget` onto the MGS `Splash_Panel_0`; `Splash_SetImageJpeg` builds a runtime `leImage` (format JPEG) from the in-memory bytes.
- **`ui/loader.{c,h}`** — one-shot boot task (self-deletes): mount → read JPEG (≤1 MB, baseline) → set image → `Video_EnableBacklight` → min-hold → `UiManager_ShowDashboard` → video go-live.
- **`ui_manager`** — BASE canvas starts 32bpp (`s_fb_splash`); `screenShow_Splash` + `Splash_AttachImage` at init; `screenShow_Dashboard` deferred; `UiManager_ShowDashboard()` hides splash, swaps the canvas to RGB565 `s_fb_base`, shows dashboard. No layer-mode override (MGS screens assert their own).
- **`video`** — `XLCDC_EnableBacklight` moved out of `video_task` into `Video_EnableBacklight()`; capture/display go-live moved to the loader.
- **`app.c`** — `Loader_Start()`; early video go-live removed.
- **`user.cmake`** — added `loader.c` + `screen_splash.c`. **`data/ui/splash.jpg`** — 1280×800 placeholder.
- MGS `le_gen_screen_Splash.{c,h}` (your regen, RGBA8888) is compiled by the generated build automatically.

**Before you test:** copy `data/ui/splash.jpg` to the card at `/ui/splash.jpg` (or it'll show the panel's solid-fill fallback). I couldn't compile here, so this is code-complete pending your build.

**Bring-up gates / risks** (documented in `ui_compositor.md` §10/§12):
1. **Runtime JPEG-from-SD decode into the 32bpp canvas** — the load-bearing unknown; if it works, album-art preload is de-risked too. Decoder is **baseline JPEG only** (the placeholder is baseline).
2. **Splash→dashboard is a hard cut** — possible 1-frame flash as BASE swaps to the not-yet-painted RGB565 buffer.
3. **Backlight uses a fixed settle delay** (`SPLASH_RENDER_SETTLE_MS=500`), not a real paint-complete signal — tune if the panel lights mid-decode.

The **Splash** MGS screen is set to `RGBA_8888` (so `screenShow_Splash` asserts the matching Legato layer mode) and the **Dashboard** stays `RGB_565`, so `ui_manager` needs no layer-mode override — just the `gfxcSetPixelBuffer` buffer swap at the handoff. Canvas count stays 3 (splash reuses the BASE slot). Missing/oversized/no-card → the panel's solid fill is the fallback. Seed `data/ui/splash.jpg` (placeholder). JPEG over BMP/RAW: BMP isn't Legato-decodable (only RAW/JPEG/PNG), so it would mean a custom parser + bypassing the `leImageWidget` path and would prove nothing reusable; JPEG reuses Legato's enabled decoder and **is** the album-art pre-load path. RGB888-without-hoops confirmed in `gfx_canvas.c` (per-canvas mode auto-configures the XLCDC layer), so the splash gets full color depth while the steady-state dashboard stays RGB565 to save DDR bandwidth; the 32bpp splash buffer doubles as future album-art decode scratch. Splash kept as an MGS shell (Greg's call) for base-view uniformity even though its only real content is the loaded image; the image widget is code-added since it's runtime data. Loader is a task (not `APP_Initialize`) because SD mount + FatFs + decode block on I/O and need the scheduler. That detail is the key — it reframes the whole diagnosis. This isn't a color-mode/stride bug at all: **it's incomplete first-paint shown over uninitialized DRAM.** When a screen is revealed (or the backlight is already on), Legato hasn't finished painting its tree yet, and fresh RAM is noise — so you see noise → progressive fill → settle. That single cause explains every symptom: yellow (uninitialized 32bpp DRAM), garbled splash (mid-decode/mid-paint), dashboard top-1/3 noise (paint not done), nav noise on open (same). The 32bpp↔565 switch was a red herring.

Your direction is exactly right — and it's actually the *original* compositor vision (doc §1: "showing a panel = point a layer at its surface; no re-render"). Let me ground a plan against the real canvas budget and the MGS persistent behavior before I write it up.

Now I understand the full picture — and it reframes everything. Two key facts from the code:

- **`CONFIG_CANVAS_NUM_OBJ = 8`** but `LE_LAYER_COUNT = 3` — the canvas framework has room for **8 surfaces**, far more than the 3 Legato layers. So per-screen surfaces are feasible.
- **Every screen is currently non-persistent**: `screenHide_*` calls `leWidget_Delete(root0)` and NULLs all ~250 widget pointers. So every show **rebuilds the entire tree and repaints from scratch** — and the Dashboard tree is huge (200+ widgets), which is exactly why it takes "a second or two" to fully paint.

**Corrected diagnosis (single root cause):** there's no color-mode/stride bug. It's **reveal-before-paint over uninitialized DRAM**. We make a canvas visible (backlight already on) while Legato is still incrementally painting its freshly-rebuilt tree; unpainted regions show fresh-RAM noise → progressive fill → settle. Yellow splash, garbled splash, dashboard top-1/3 noise, nav noise — all the same cause.

Your direction is the correct fix and it's the original compositor vision (doc §1). Let me note it and lay out the architecture.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-26 21:09:48Z)**_

Noted in the journal and compositor doc. Here's where this leaves us.

## The fix has two layers

**Interim (cheap, makes the current build presentable now):** `memset` each canvas surface to its background color before first reveal. The noise is just uninitialized DRAM showing through not-yet-painted regions — clearing to black (or the scheme bg) turns "RAM noise → progressive paint" into "clean solid → content fills in," which reads like a normal app load. ~5 lines, low risk, no MGS changes.

**Proper (your direction — pre-render + persistent):**
- **Persistent widgets** (your MGS find): set each screen persistent so `screenHide` stops deleting the tree and `screenShow` stops rebuilding it. That's your action in Composer + regen.
- **Per-screen canvas + pre-render**: paint each screen into its own surface (8 available) and switch by re-pointing the layer — no repaint on switch. Crucially, **pre-paint the heavy Dashboard during the splash's ≥1.2 s hold**, so the swap reveals a finished screen instead of a 1–2 s fill-in.

## The hard part to design (why I want to plan, not charge in)

Legato only has 3 layers and renders attached roots into *their* layer's canvas. To paint a screen into its own off-screen surface while another is visible, we need either a spare Legato layer or `gfxcSetBaseCanvasID` multiplexing across the 8 canvas objects — plus a safe "render-to-completion-then-reveal" step that doesn't race `LEGATO_Tasks`. And live-telemetry screens (Dashboard) still repaint while shown, so persistence covers the *first reveal* and switch-back, not steady state. None of this is hard to get wrong-but-untestable-here, so I'd rather design it deliberately.

## Recommendation

1. Let me apply the **interim memset** now so your current build looks clean while we design the real thing.
2. You set the screens **persistent** in MGS + regen (your lever).
3. I write up the **pre-render/multiplexing plan** for review before implementing.

Want me to do the memset mitigation now and start the pre-render plan? Or skip the interim and go straight to designing the persistent/pre-render architecture?

```text
leResult leUpdate(uint32_t dt)
{
#if LE_DRIVER_LAYER_MODE == 1
    uint32_t itr;
    gfxIOCTLArg_LayerRect layerRect;
    leState* state;
    leLayerState* layerState;
#endif

    leEvent_ProcessEvents();

#if LE_DRIVER_LAYER_MODE == 1
    state = leGetState();

    for(itr = 0; itr < state->layerList.size; ++itr)
    {
        layerRect.layer.id = itr;
        layerRect.x = 0;
        layerRect.y = 0;
        layerRect.width = 0;
        layerRect.height = 0;

        leRenderer_DisplayInterface()->ioctl(GFX_IOCTL_GET_LAYER_RECT, &layerRect);
        layerState = (leLayerState*)leList_Get(&state->layerList, itr);

        layerState->driverPosition.x = layerRect.x;
        layerState->driverPosition.y = layerRect.y;

        layerState->root.fn->setPosition(&layerState->root,
                                         0,
                                         0);

#if LE_RENDER_ORIENTATION == 90 || LE_RENDER_ORIENTATION == 270
        layerState->root.fn->setSize(&layerState->root,
                                     layerRect.height,
                                     layerRect.width);
#else
        layerState->root.fn->setSize(&layerState->root,
                                     layerRect.width,
                                     layerRect.height);
#endif
    }
#endif

#if LE_STREAMING_ENABLED == 1
    // there is an active stream in progress, service that to completion
    // before painting anything else
    if(_state.activeStream != NULL)
    {
        if(_state.activeStream->isDone(_state.activeStream) == LE_TRUE)
        {
            _state.activeStream = NULL;
        }
        else
        {
            _state.activeStream->exec(_state.activeStream);

            return LE_SUCCESS;
        }
    }
```

I now have everything needed and your plan is sound. Key refinements from what I found in the code, which make it deterministic:

1. **`leUpdate(0)` returns only when fully painted** (preemption 0 + synchronous GFX2D blit). So "force full draw, once done" = one `leUpdate(0)` call — no polling.
2. **Suspend `LEGATO_Tasks` during boot** and let the loader drive `leUpdate` itself (both `INCLUDE_vTaskSuspend`/`xTaskGetHandle` are on). That makes the off-screen pre-paint race-free, vs. fighting the MCC render task.
3. **Layer map** (each screen its own Legato-layer/canvas, no multiplex): Splash → layer 2 / canvas 2 / **OVR2** (32bpp, full screen, on top); Dashboard → layer 0 / canvas 0 / **BASE** (RGB565); Nav → layer 1 / canvas 1 / **OVR1** (already does this).

Sequence: build+show splash on OVR2 (backlight off) → loader suspends LEGATO → paint splash (`leUpdate`) → backlight on (splash up, complete) → build dashboard+nav on BASE/OVR1 *under* the splash → `leUpdate` paints them fully (hidden) → hide OVR2 to reveal the finished dashboard → resume LEGATO. Exactly your "splash up first, draw the rest behind it," now with deterministic completion.

```c
#include "ui/screens/splash/screen_splash.h"

#include <stdint.h>

#include "definitions.h"   /* XLCDC_EnableBacklight */
#include "gfx/canvas/gfx_canvas_api.h"
#include "gfx/legato/legato.h"
#include "gfx/legato/generated/le_gen_assets.h"
#include "gfx/legato/generated/screen/le_gen_screen_Dashboard.h"
#include "gfx/legato/generated/screen/le_gen_screen_Navigation.h"
#include "gfx/legato/generated/screen/le_gen_screen_Splash.h"

/* Each screen gets its own canvas surface (Legato layer index == canvas id,
 * baseCanvasID 0) and renders into it independently — no shared buffer, no
 * runtime re-point. Screens are persistent (built once, never torn down), so a
 * surface holds its last-painted pixels and switching screens is just mapping
 * the surface's canvas to a hardware layer.
 *
 * XLCDC layer indices (drvLayer/layerOrder): BASE 0, HEO 1, OVR1 2, OVR2 3 —
 * HEO is the live camera (off-limits). OVR2 is the topmost overlay; the boot
 * splash uses it so it can be drawn full-screen over the BASE dashboard while
 * the dashboard paints underneath, then dropped to reveal the finished screen. */
#define CANVAS_DASH    0u   /* Legato layer 0 → HW BASE, RGB565  */
#define CANVAS_NAV     1u   /* Legato layer 1 → HW OVR1 (owned by ui/nav) */
#define CANVAS_SPLASH  2u   /* Legato layer 2 → HW OVR2, RGBA8888 */

#define HW_BASE   0u
#define HW_OVR2   3u

#define BASE_W   1280u
#define BASE_H    800u

#define FB_NOCACHE   __attribute__((section(".region_nocache"), aligned (32)))

/* Per-screen surfaces, non-cached so the 2D engine and LCDC DMA read CPU-
 * rendered pixels coherently (matches FB_CACHE_NC). The dashboard is RGB565
 * (steady-state UI needs no more); the splash is 32bpp so the photo keeps full
 * color depth. The splash buffer is also the natural decode scratch for the
 * (future) album-art pre-load, once the splash leaves the screen. */
static uint16_t FB_NOCACHE s_fb_base[BASE_W * BASE_H];
static uint32_t FB_NOCACHE s_fb_splash[BASE_W * BASE_H];

void UiManager_Initialize(void)
{
    /* Assign the per-screen canvas surfaces before the canvas runs. The nav owns
     * its own (canvas 1, via Nav_InitSurface). */
    gfxcSetPixelBuffer(CANVAS_DASH,   BASE_W, BASE_H, GFX_COLOR_MODE_RGB_565,   s_fb_base);
    gfxcSetPixelBuffer(CANVAS_SPLASH, BASE_W, BASE_H, GFX_COLOR_MODE_RGBA_8888, s_fb_splash);
    Nav_InitSurface();

    /* Drive the canvas state machine to RUNNING now, before the scheduler, so a
     * blit into a canvas is not dropped by the RUNNING gate in GFXC_BlitBuffer. */
    GFX_CANVAS_Task();

    leSetStringTable(&stringTable);
    initializeStrings();

    /* Build + host ONLY the splash here; the dashboard and nav are built later by
     * the loader (UiManager_BuildMainScreens), painted off-screen behind the
     * splash. screenInit_Splash builds the MGS tree and attaches its root to its
     * authored layer 0 — re-host that onto layer 2 (canvas 2 → OVR2), add the
     * image widget, and bind the canvas to the OVR2 hardware layer. Nothing is
     * painted and the backlight is off; the loader drives the first paint. */
    screenInit_Splash();
    leWidget *sp = screenGetRoot_Splash(0);
    leRemoveRootWidget(sp, 0);
    leAddRootWidget(sp, CANVAS_SPLASH);
    leSetLayerColorMode(CANVAS_SPLASH, LE_COLOR_MODE_RGBA_8888);
    Splash_AttachImage();

    gfxcSetWindowPosition(CANVAS_SPLASH, 0, 0);
    gfxcSetWindowSize(CANVAS_SPLASH, BASE_W, BASE_H);
    gfxcSetLayer(CANVAS_SPLASH, HW_OVR2);
    gfxcShowCanvas(CANVAS_SPLASH);
    gfxcCanvasUpdate(CANVAS_SPLASH);
}

/* Build the main screens onto their own layers/canvases. Called by the loader
 * (with LEGATO_Tasks suspended) after the splash is up, so their first paint
 * happens off-screen behind the splash. Dashboard stays on its authored layer 0
 * (canvas 0 → BASE); Navigation_OnShow re-hosts the nav onto layer 1 (OVR1).
 * Init+show are paired so the nav's re-host completes before the loader paints
 * (otherwise both roots would briefly share layer 0). */
void UiManager_BuildMainScreens(void)
{
    screenInit_Dashboard();
    screenShow_Dashboard();    /* Dashboard_OnShow binds canvas 0 → BASE */
    screenInit_Navigation();
    screenShow_Navigation();   /* Navigation_OnShow re-hosts nav → OVR1 */
}

/* Reveal the (already painted, behind-the-splash) dashboard by dropping the
 * splash overlay. The dashboard canvas is already bound to BASE and full; hiding
 * OVR2 uncovers it instantly. Called by the loader after the main screens are
 * painted. */
void UiManager_RevealDashboard(void)
{
    gfxcHideCanvas(CANVAS_SPLASH);
    gfxcCanvasUpdate(CANVAS_SPLASH);
}

/* Turn on the LCD backlight. Deferred out of video-task init so the boot loader
 * lights the panel only after the splash is painted (no pre-splash garbage
 * frame). The UI owns the display/composition, so backlight lives here, not in
 * video. Idempotent register write; callable from any task. */
void UiManager_EnableBacklight(void)
{
    XLCDC_EnableBacklight();
}

/* Dashboard screen composition root (declared in le_gen_screen_Dashboard.h).
 * Binds the dashboard to its BASE layer. The nav drawer is its own screen
 * (Navigation), hosted by ui/nav from its own OnShow hook. */
void Dashboard_OnShow(void)
{
    gfxcSetWindowPosition(CANVAS_DASH, 0, 0);
    gfxcSetWindowSize(CANVAS_DASH, BASE_W, BASE_H);
    gfxcSetLayer(CANVAS_DASH, HW_BASE);
    gfxcShowCanvas(CANVAS_DASH);
    gfxcCanvasUpdate(CANVAS_DASH);
}
```

```text
51	static uint32_t load_splash_file(void)
52	{
53	    if (!Storage_Mount()) { return 0u; }
54	
55	    char path[64];
56	    (void)snprintf(path, sizeof(path), "%s%s", Storage_MountPoint(), SPLASH_REL_PATH);

59	    if (h == SYS_FS_HANDLE_INVALID)

72	    }
73	
74	    uint32_t total = 0u;
75	    bool err = false;
76	    while (total < (uint32_t)sz)
77	    {
78	        size_t want = (size_t)((uint32_t)sz - total);
79	        if (want > SPLASH_READ_CHUNK) { want = SPLASH_READ_CHUNK; }
```

```text
222	- **Reveal-before-paint (the big one — drives the next architecture step).** Screens are shown
223	  while Legato is still incrementally painting their freshly-rebuilt trees, so unpainted regions
224	  flash uninitialized-DRAM noise before settling (the Dashboard's ~200-widget tree takes ~1–2 s to
225	  fully software-paint). Today every MGS screen is **non-persistent** (`screenHide` deletes the
226	  tree; every show rebuilds + repaints from scratch). **Target:** pre-render each screen into its
227	  own canvas surface (the framework allows 8, `CONFIG_CANVAS_NUM_OBJ`) and make the MGS screens
228	  **persistent**, so switching is a layer re-point with no rebuild/repaint — the §1 "show = point a
229	  layer at its surface" model. Caveats to resolve: live-telemetry screens still repaint while
230	  shown; only 3 Legato layers exist so off-screen pre-paint needs a spare layer or
231	  `gfxcSetBaseCanvasID` multiplexing; and a safe "render-to-completion-then-reveal" mechanism vs
232	  `LEGATO_Tasks`. Cheap interim: `memset` each surface to its background color before first reveal
233	  so the gap is a clean solid, not noise.
234	- **`manual_input.c` fate** — `Screen0` retired; the strum handlers now serve the Dashboard
235	  screen, so it stays until manual control is reworked.
236	- **Per-pixel alpha** — which (if any) overlay needs ARGB8888 over the camera vs. layer alpha.
237	
238	## 10a. Anti-aliased rounded button corners (done)
239	
240	The nav buttons use the widget `cornerRadius` (set in code — not exposed in MGS), but the
241	classic skin's rounded-rect fill draws corners with `leRenderer_ArcFill` (hard, stepped
242	edges). Smoothing is done **without touching Legato/MCC code** (`config/default/` is
243	off-limits), via a per-instance vtable re-point in `src/ui/widgets/button_aa/widget_button_aa.c`:
244	
245	- `leWidget.fn` is a writable per-instance pointer to a `const` vtable. `ButtonAA_Enable`
246	  makes one shared writable copy of the button vtable, overrides only `_paint`, and points
247	  the button's `fn`/`widget.fn` at it. No `LE_DYNAMIC_VTABLES` (not an MCC knob; unguarded
248	  `#define 0` in generated `legato_config.h`), no global RAM cost — scoped to re-pointed
249	  buttons.
250	- The wrapper runs the original paint (bg + label + border), then on `DONE` with the
251	  supported radius overdraws the four corners: sample the backdrop from each corner's
252	  extreme pixel (left untouched by the rounded fill), then blend a 1px transition band from
253	  a precomputed coverage mask via `leColorLerp` + `leRenderer_PutPixel`. Fill is read from
254	  the live scheme each paint, so highlight (selected/unselected) and pressed states track.
255	- Runs **in-pass** (damage → repaint → AA in one paint), so no timing/flicker window.
256	- Wired from `nav_buttons_init()`; currently nav-only. Extending app-wide is just calling
257	  `ButtonAA_Enable` from other screens' button init. Single radius (`BUTTON_AA_RADIUS`);
258	  other radii pass through unsmoothed.
259	
260	## 12. Boot splash (done — code-complete, pending hardware test)
261	
262	A full-screen photo splash is the first thing on the panel: the loader reads it off the SD card
263	into RAM, gets it onto BASE, and only then lights the backlight, so the panel never shows a
264	pre-splash/garbage frame. It's also the first real use of the **replace** verb (§5) and proves
265	the runtime-image path the album-art pre-load will reuse.
266	
267	- **Splash is a base view on BASE (canvas 0), with an MGS shell.** The `Splash` MGS screen
268	  (`le_gen_screen_Splash.c`: a full-screen `Splash_Panel_0` with a solid scheme fill) is the base
269	  — kept for the "every base view has an MGS component" convention, even though the splash's only
270	  real content is loaded, not authored. The photo can't be an MGS asset (runtime SD read), so
271	  `screens/splash/screen_splash.c` adds one `leImageWidget` onto `Splash_Panel_0` in code and
272	  points it at the in-memory JPEG; the panel's solid fill is the **fallback "splash"** when there's
273	  no card/image. `ui_manager` shows the splash on BASE at init and defers `screenShow_Dashboard`
```

Implemented. The architecture is now your plan, made deterministic:

## What changed

**`ui_manager`** — each screen owns its canvas/Legato-layer/HW-layer, no multiplex:
- Dashboard → layer 0 / canvas 0 / **BASE** (RGB565)
- Nav → layer 1 / canvas 1 / **OVR1** (RGB565, unchanged)
- Splash → layer 2 / canvas 2 / **OVR2** (RGBA8888, full-screen, topmost)
- `UiManager_Initialize` builds + hosts only the splash (backlight off). New `UiManager_BuildMainScreens()` (build dashboard+nav) and `UiManager_RevealDashboard()` (drop OVR2) replace the old BASE-swap. The RGB565↔8888 swap is gone — splash has its own 32bpp OVR2 canvas.

**`loader`** — owns `leUpdate` during boot (priority 3, suspends `LEGATO_Tasks`):
`suspend LEGATO → load JPEG + leUpdate (splash painted) → backlight on → BuildMainScreens + leUpdate (dashboard+nav painted behind the OVR2 splash) → min hold → RevealDashboard → resume LEGATO → video go-live`. One `leUpdate(0)` = fully painted (preemption 0 + synchronous blit), so "once done" is deterministic — no settle delays.

Docs updated: `ui_compositor.md` §13 (the new model) + §12 (splash on OVR2), journal bring-up #2 entry + decision row.

## Bring-up risks to watch (couldn't test here)

1. **OVR2 RGBA8888 opacity** — the #1 thing to check. If the OVR2 hardware layer does per-pixel alpha blending and Legato leaves the alpha byte at 0, the splash would be *transparent* (you'd see the dashboard through it). The splash panel + image are opaque fills so Legato should write α=0xFF, but if the splash looks see-through/blended, the fix is forcing OVR2 to opaque/global-alpha. (This is the §10 "per-pixel alpha" open item, now live.)
2. **Z-order** — assumes OVR2 sits above BASE by default (standard XLCDC). If the splash doesn't cover the dashboard, that's the cause.
3. **`xTaskGetHandle("LEGATO_Tasks")`** — exact MCC task name; if it returns NULL the loader logs nothing but skips suspend (paints would race). Worth confirming the name on hardware.

Everything's code-complete pending your build + flash. Given the OVR2-alpha uncertainty, that's the first thing to eyeball when it comes up. Want me to hold here for the hardware run before any commit?

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-26 21:50:26Z)**_

Let me answer your streaming question definitively first — the JPEG decoder source settles it:

**No, you don't need the streaming interface.** In [legato_imagedecoder_jpeg.c:49-57](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/gfx/legato/image/jpeg/legato_imagedecoder_jpeg.c#L49-L57), with `LE_STREAMING_ENABLED == 0` the decoder supports a JPEG **only** when `header.location == LE_STREAM_LOCATION_ID_INTERNAL` — i.e. the compressed bytes are resident in MCU memory, which is exactly what we do (read the whole file into `s_jpeg`, point the `leImage` at it). It then reads via `internalMemoryRead`. The streaming interface is for the *opposite* case — decoding an image that is **not** all in RAM (streamed from an external/SD source in chunks). Since we pre-load the file, leave it off.

So the magenta isn't a decode-capability problem. Let me check the two things your symptoms actually point at — the splash compositing transparently (the dashboard paint showing *through* it is the tell), and the hamburger event wiring:

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-26 21:53:45Z)**_

The nav event **is** wired (line 301 → `event_Dashboard_BUTTON_SYSYEM_NAVIGATION_OnPressed`), so that's not the problem. And I found the real splash cause:

**OVR2 uses per-pixel alpha blending.** `LCDC_OVR2CFG9` (line 374-378) sets `SFACTC=4` (= A0×As) with `A0=255` — so the *source pixel's alpha (As)* controls opacity. Your symptom — dashboard "purple lines" showing *through* the splash — is the splash being composited transparent because Legato is writing alpha≈0 into the RGBA8888 canvas (scheme/RGB fills carry no alpha → α=0 in an ARGB buffer, a classic Legato-on-ARGB gotcha). The "magenta+noise" is the uninitialized BASE/dashboard buffer showing through before it paints.

So the splash is probably decoding fine — it's just invisible. The fix is to make OVR2 **opaque** (ignore per-pixel alpha). `XLCDC_SetupOVR2Layer` is MCC-generated (off-limits), so the right move is a runtime register write from our code, exactly like `video.c` already does for HEO. Let me confirm the exact blend-factor encoding before I poke it:

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-26 22:03:02Z)**_

`JPEG_bReadHeader` pulls real dimensions from the JPEG itself, and the decoder blits per-pixel via the renderer — so stride/dims aren't the garble. The prime suspect for "garbled, nowhere close" is the **placeholder JPEG itself**: `sips` emitted it with **restart markers (DRI)** + Exif/APP13, and many compact decoders desync on restart markers → garbage after the first interval. Let me check whether this decoder handles them:

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-26 22:06:17Z)**_

**Found the real root cause.** Look at the canvas commit path (`SET_LAYER_UNLOCK`, lines 170-175): it commits address, alpha, position, size, stride, enable — but **never calls `XLCDC_SetLayerRGBColorMode`**. So `GFX_IOCTL_SET_LAYER_COLOR_MODE` only stores `drvLayer.pixelformat` and it's **never written to hardware**. The HW layer keeps whatever `XLCDC_SetupOVR2Layer` set (`RGBMODE(3)`).

So my premise that "the canvas re-sets the HW layer color mode from the buffer" was wrong for this driver. The RGB565 dashboard/nav work because BASE/OVR1's MCC default *is* RGB565 — but the **RGBA8888 splash buffer is being read by an OVR2 layer still in the project's default RGB mode → garbled**. That's why both cuts garbled, and only the 32bpp surface. Let me confirm the modes:

**That's the bug — and it's well-grounded now.** Confirmed:

- `FB_COL_MODE = XLCDC_RGB_COLOR_MODE_RGB_565`, `FB_TYPE_SZ = 2` — the driver assumes **every** layer is the RGB565 project framebuffer.
- The canvas commit path never calls `XLCDC_SetLayerRGBColorMode`, so our `RGBA_8888` request is stored in `drvLayer.pixelformat` and **dropped**. `RGBMODE(3)` = `RGB_565` (enum index 3).
- So OVR2 reads our 32bpp splash buffer **as 16bpp RGB565** → garbled + magenta-ish, exactly what you see. (This is why both cuts garbled and only on the 32bpp surface; RGB565 dashboard/nav match the default and render fine.)

The fix is one runtime register write — set OVR2's HW color mode to RGBA8888 directly (the driver never rewrites `RGBMODE`, so it sticks), the same XLCDC-poke pattern `video.c` already uses for HEO:

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-26 22:09:08Z)**_

All three symbols are declared in `plib_xlcdc.h` (reachable via `definitions.h`), so the one-line fix builds.

## Root cause (read from the driver, not guessed)

The garble wasn't the JPEG or alpha — it's a **GFX-XLCDC driver limitation**: its canvas commit path (`drv_gfx_xlcdc.c` `SET_LAYER_UNLOCK`) writes address/alpha/position/size/stride/enable but **never `RGBMODE`**. It assumes every layer is the project framebuffer format (`FB_COL_MODE = RGB565`, 2 bytes/pixel). So when the canvas requested RGBA8888 for the splash, it was stored in `drvLayer.pixelformat` and **silently dropped** — OVR2 stayed RGB565 and read our 32bpp buffer as 16bpp → garbled/magenta. RGB565 dashboard and nav matched the default, which is exactly why only the splash garbled, in both cuts.

**Fix:** one line in `ui_manager` — `XLCDC_SetLayerRGBColorMode(XLCDC_LAYER_OVR2, RGBA_8888, true)` after binding the splash canvas. The driver never rewrites `RGBMODE`, so it sticks (same runtime XLCDC poke `video.c` already uses for HEO). My earlier claim that "the canvas re-sets the HW layer mode" was wrong for this driver — corrected in the docs.

**And your streaming question:** No, not needed. The decoder supports memory-resident JPEGs (`LE_STREAM_LOCATION_ID_INTERNAL`) with streaming off; streaming is only for images not fully in RAM. I also confirmed the decoder handles restart markers + standard subsampling and skips the Exif/APP13 cruft by length — so the placeholder JPEG should decode fine once OVR2 is in the right mode.

## Two things to check after you rebuild

1. **Opacity** — if the splash now renders correctly but looks blended/see-through, that's the OVR2 per-pixel-alpha (`OVR2CFG9` SFACTC=A0×As); it's fine if the decoder writes α=0xFF. Heads-up: `XLCDC_SetLayerOpts` rewrites `CFG9` on every canvas commit, so the fix there (if needed) is opaque *pixels*, not a register poke.
2. **Nav hamburger** — the event *is* wired (`le_gen_screen_Dashboard.c:301`), so if it still does nothing after the garble fix, it's the input/pick path; I'll add a debug log to the `OnPressed` handler and trace touch. It may also just have been collateral from the broken splash state.

Rebuild with the RGBMODE fix and let's see how far it gets — I expect a clean splash now. Want me to dig into the nav button in parallel, or wait for the rebuild?

Confirmed, and your read is exactly right. `LE_SCRATCH_BUFFER_COUNT = 1` is the key: in `preRect` (line 632-633), if the single scratch buffer is still **locked** (its previous tile not yet committed to the canvas), the renderer just `return`s. The scratch is unlocked by the canvas commit — which runs in `GFX_CANVAS_Task`, a priority-2 task that **can't run while the loader (priority 3) is sitting in `leUpdate`**. So my one `leUpdate(0)` renders exactly one scratch tile (~131072 px @ 32bpp ≈ the region you see), locks the buffer, and returns. The other ~7 tiles never get a chance.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-26 22:20:26Z)**_

Yes to both your questions — that was the bug, and your instinct nailed it.

**Confirmed:** `LE_SCRATCH_BUFFER_SIZE_KB = 512`, `LE_SCRATCH_BUFFER_COUNT = 1`. At 32bpp that scratch holds `512KB·8/32 = 131,072` px — about the ~400×300 region you saw. The full screen is ~8 of those tiles. And yes — my single `leUpdate(0)` was treated as "done" after the first tile: `preRect` renders one tile into the scratch, locks it, and **bails on the next tile because the scratch is still locked**. The scratch is freed by the canvas commit in `GFX_CANVAS_Task` — a priority-2 task that couldn't run while the loader (priority 3) sat in that one `leUpdate`. So one tile, then return. My "one `leUpdate` = full frame" assumption was simply wrong.

**Fix:** `loader.c` now has `render_to_idle()` — it loops `leUpdate(0)` + `GFX_CANVAS_Task()` (commit tile, free scratch) until the public `leRenderer_IsIdle()` reports the frame complete (`LE_FRAME_READY`), capped at 64 iterations. Both paint points (splash, then dashboard+nav) use it. Docs corrected (I'd repeated the wrong claim in §13 + the journal — fixed).

One heads-up for when it comes up: **a full-screen JPEG gets re-decoded per scratch tile (~8×)**, since JPEG isn't random-access — so the splash render will take a noticeable beat (it's one-time, hidden behind nothing since it *is* the splash). If that's too slow, the clean optimization is a bigger scratch buffer (enough for one full-screen tile → decode once), which is an MGS Graphics-settings change + a few MB of nocache RAM. I'd leave it until we see whether the speed actually bothers you.

Rebuild and the splash should fill the whole screen now. Still on my list once this is confirmed: the nav hamburger (event's wired, so it's input/pick — I'll trace it next).

Calling `GFX_CANVAS_Task()` directly in a tight loop doesn't actually free the scratch (the canvas commit completes asynchronously — it needs real task scheduling/time, not a busy-loop), so all 64 iterations bail with the scratch still locked → one tile. Suspending LEGATO was the root mistake: it forced me to re-implement, badly, what the normal task interplay already does correctly (the dashboard renders fully in steady state precisely because LEGATO_Tasks and GFX_CANVAS_Task interleave with real yields).

The clean design is exactly what you said: **don't touch the scheduler. Build the screens, then just pend on `leRenderer_IsIdle()`** while the normal tasks render. No suspend, no loader-driven `leUpdate`, no priority games. Let me rework it.

```c
#include "ui/loader.h"

#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>

#include "FreeRTOS.h"
#include "task.h"

#include "definitions.h"
#include "log.h"
#include "storage/storage.h"
#include "video/video.h"
#include "ui/ui_manager.h"
#include "ui/screens/splash/screen_splash.h"
#include "gfx/legato/renderer/legato_renderer.h"  /* leRenderer_IsIdle */

#define LOADER_TASK_STACK_WORDS  1024u
#define LOADER_TASK_PRIORITY     2u    /* UI band; blocks on SD I/O + the render wait */

#define SPLASH_REL_PATH    "/ui/splash.jpg"
#define SPLASH_JPEG_MAX    (1024u * 1024u)   /* cap; skip splash if file is larger */
#define SPLASH_READ_CHUNK  (64u * 1024u)

#define SPLASH_MIN_MS              1200u  /* hold the splash at least this long */
#define RENDER_START_TIMEOUT_MS    200u  /* wait for the render task to pick up the damage */
#define RENDER_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS    8000u  /* bound the full-paint wait so a stall can't hang boot */

/* Video window: 720×480 video at (280, 76) on the 1280×800 panel — 1:1 with the
 * bridge's typical 480p source, leaving a UI strip below. */
#define VIDEO_WIN_X   280u
#define VIDEO_WIN_Y    76u
#define VIDEO_WIN_W   720u
#define VIDEO_WIN_H   480u

/* Compressed splash JPEG, read from SD. Static (off-stack); the leImage handed
 * to Legato points straight at it, so it must stay resident while the splash is
 * shown. Cache-line aligned for the FatFs multi-block read fast path. */
static uint8_t s_jpeg[SPLASH_JPEG_MAX] __ALIGNED(CACHE_LINE_SIZE);

static StackType_t  s_task_stack[LOADER_TASK_STACK_WORDS];
static StaticTask_t s_task_tcb;

/* Read the splash file into s_jpeg. Returns byte count, or 0 on any failure
 * (no card, missing file, too large, short read) — caller falls back to the
 * splash's solid fill. */
static uint32_t load_splash_file(void)
{
    if (!Storage_Mount()) { return 0u; }

    char path[64];
    (void)snprintf(path, sizeof(path), "%s%s", Storage_MountPoint(), SPLASH_REL_PATH);

    SYS_FS_HANDLE h = SYS_FS_FileOpen(path, SYS_FS_FILE_OPEN_READ);
    if (h == SYS_FS_HANDLE_INVALID)
    {
        LOG_WARN("LOADER: no splash %s (fs err %d)\r\n", path, (int)SYS_FS_Error());
        return 0u;
    }

    int32_t sz = SYS_FS_FileSize(h);
    if (sz <= 0 || (uint32_t)sz > SPLASH_JPEG_MAX)
    {
        LOG_WARN("LOADER: splash size %ld invalid (cap %u)\r\n",
                 (long)sz, (unsigned)SPLASH_JPEG_MAX);
        (void)SYS_FS_FileClose(h);
        return 0u;
    }

    uint32_t total = 0u;
    bool err = false;
    while (total < (uint32_t)sz)
    {
        size_t want = (size_t)((uint32_t)sz - total);
        if (want > SPLASH_READ_CHUNK) { want = SPLASH_READ_CHUNK; }

        size_t got = SYS_FS_FileRead(h, &s_jpeg[total], want);
        if (got == 0u || got == (size_t)-1) { err = true; break; }
        total += (uint32_t)got;
    }
    (void)SYS_FS_FileClose(h);

    if (err || total != (uint32_t)sz)
    {
        LOG_WARN("LOADER: splash read short %lu/%ld\r\n", (unsigned long)total, (long)sz);
        return 0u;
    }
    LOG_INFO("LOADER: splash %lu B loaded\r\n", (unsigned long)total);
    return total;
}

/* Block until the Legato render task has fully painted all pending damage.
 *
 * We do NOT drive leUpdate ourselves — the normal LEGATO_Tasks + GFX_CANVAS_Task
 * pair renders the full screen correctly (a full-screen surface spans several
 * scratch tiles, and the scratch is freed by the canvas commit between render
 * passes; that only happens when those tasks actually run). So the loader just
 * yields and polls the public idle flag. First wait for the task to pick up the
 * queued damage (go busy), then wait for it to finish — both bounded so a render
 * stall can't hang boot. */
static void wait_render_idle(void)
{
    TickType_t start = xTaskGetTickCount();
    while (leRenderer_IsIdle() &&
           (xTaskGetTickCount() - start) < pdMS_TO_TICKS(RENDER_START_TIMEOUT_MS))
    {
        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(4));
    }

    start = xTaskGetTickCount();
    while (!leRenderer_IsIdle())
    {
        if ((xTaskGetTickCount() - start) >= pdMS_TO_TICKS(RENDER_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS))
        {
            LOG_WARN("LOADER: render-idle wait timed out\r\n");
            return;
        }
        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(4));
    }
}

static void loader_task(void *param)
{
    (void)param;

    /* The splash, dashboard, and nav were built + hosted on their own layers by
     * UiManager_Initialize (pre-scheduler); the Legato render task is now
     * painting them (backlight still off). Load the splash image, wait for the
     * render to finish, then light the panel — the first lit frame is the
     * fully-painted splash, with the dashboard finished behind it on BASE. No
     * image (no card / too large) → the panel's solid fill is the fallback. */
    uint32_t len = load_splash_file();
    if (!((len > 0u) && Splash_SetImageJpeg(s_jpeg, len)))
    {
        LOG_WARN("LOADER: solid-fill splash (no image)\r\n");
    }

    wait_render_idle();
    UiManager_EnableBacklight();
    TickType_t shown_at = xTaskGetTickCount();

    /* --- Asset pre-load goes here (album art → DDR cache, etc.). The 32bpp
     * splash buffer (ui_manager) is free to reuse as decode scratch once the
     * splash leaves the screen. None yet. --- */

    /* Hold the splash a minimum time so a fast boot doesn't flash it away. */
    TickType_t elapsed   = xTaskGetTickCount() - shown_at;
    TickType_t min_ticks = pdMS_TO_TICKS(SPLASH_MIN_MS);
    if (elapsed < min_ticks) { vTaskDelay(min_ticks - elapsed); }

    /* Drop the splash → the dashboard (painted behind it) is revealed, complete.
     * Then bring the camera up. */
    UiManager_RevealDashboard();
    Video_SetWindow(VIDEO_WIN_X, VIDEO_WIN_Y, VIDEO_WIN_W, VIDEO_WIN_H);
    Video_CaptureEnable();
    Video_DisplayShow();

    vTaskDelete(NULL);
}

void Loader_Start(void)
{
    (void)xTaskCreateStatic(loader_task, "LoaderTask", LOADER_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
                            NULL, LOADER_TASK_PRIORITY, s_task_stack, &s_task_tcb);
}
```

```text
300	- **Off-screen paint to completion — pump, don't single-shot.** A *single* `leUpdate(0)` does NOT
301	  fully paint a full-screen surface: there's one scratch buffer (`LE_SCRATCH_BUFFER_COUNT = 1`,
302	  512 KB ⇒ `maxScratchPixels = 512KB·8/bpp` ≈ 131 072 px @ 32bpp), so the renderer crops the damage
303	  into ~8 scratch tiles and `preRect` bails when the scratch is still locked from the previous tile.
304	  The scratch is freed by the canvas commit in `GFX_CANVAS_Task`. So the loader's `render_to_idle()`
305	  loops `leUpdate(0)` + `GFX_CANVAS_Task()` until `leRenderer_IsIdle()` (frame == `LE_FRAME_READY`),
306	  capped for safety. (Consequence: a full-screen JPEG is re-decoded per tile — slow but one-time;
307	  a bigger scratch would decode once, at a RAM cost.)
308	- **The loader owns `leUpdate` during boot.** It runs at priority 3 (above `LEGATO_Tasks`' 2),
309	  suspends `LEGATO_Tasks` first thing (`xTaskGetHandle` + `vTaskSuspend`, both enabled), drives the
310	  paints itself (no reentrancy), and resumes the render task for steady state. Boot sequence:
311	  suspend LEGATO → load JPEG, `Splash_SetImageJpeg`, `render_to_idle` (splash fully painted) →
312	  `UiManager_EnableBacklight` (first lit frame = complete splash) → `UiManager_BuildMainScreens`,
313	  `render_to_idle` (Dashboard+Nav fully painted, hidden behind the OVR2 splash) → *(asset pre-load —
314	  none yet)* → min on-screen hold → `UiManager_RevealDashboard` (hide OVR2 → finished Dashboard) →
315	  resume LEGATO → video go-live → self-delete.
316	- **Open:** the splash stays attached to layer 2 after reveal (just hidden); the future modal dialog
317	  (also OVR2/layer 2) will need to detach it first. Touch injection during the suspended-LEGATO
318	  boot window is unguarded, but the panel is dark/splash-only then so it's not a practical race.
319	
320	## 11. Relationship to spec §4.5 / Q5
321	
322	This answers spec **Q5** (Legato vs. custom UI) for the *presentation* layer: **Legato is the
323	renderer; a marvin `ui_manager` over GFX Canvas owns surface/layer composition and screen
324	orchestration.** Per-screen *authoring* stays in MGS (one Screen per panel); the compositor
325	assembles their trees onto hardware layers.
```

Done — reworked to the clean design, no scheduler games.

## What changed

**`ui_manager.c`** — `UiManager_Initialize` now builds and hosts **all** screens pre-scheduler (splash→OVR2, dashboard→BASE, nav→OVR1). That's safe because no tasks are running yet, so there's zero concurrency to defend against. Dropped `UiManager_BuildMainScreens`.

**`loader.c`** — no longer suspends `LEGATO_Tasks`, no longer drives `leUpdate`, priority back to 2. It just: load JPEG → `Splash_SetImageJpeg` → `wait_render_idle()` (pend on the public `leRenderer_IsIdle()` — wait to go busy, then wait to finish, both bounded) → backlight on → hold → reveal → video. The normal `LEGATO_Tasks`/`GFX_CANVAS_Task` pair does the rendering, exactly as it does in steady state — which is the whole point: that interplay frees the scratch between passes and paints all the tiles, something my busy-loop could never do.

You were right on both counts:
- **Suspending the task was the wrong instinct** — it made me re-implement the render loop badly. Removed entirely.
- **The pump didn't even work** because `GFX_CANVAS_Task()` in a tight loop doesn't free the scratch (the commit needs real task scheduling between passes). Pending on idle lets that happen naturally.

Docs updated (§13 + journal bring-up #5) including an explicit "earlier mistake (corrected)" note so the dead-end is on record.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-26 22:48:34Z)**_

Clean. Two targeted fixes, both honoring the no-scheduler-hacking principle:

**1. The render race (your diagnosis).** `leRenderer_IsIdle()` is just `frameState == LE_FRAME_READY`, which is true in the ~10 ms gaps *between* `leUpdate` calls while a multi-frame paint is still going. My old wait bailed on the first idle sample → one frame's worth lit. Now `wait_render_idle` requires idle to hold **continuously for ≥120 ms** (≫ the 10 ms tick); any frame starting resets the streak, bounded by an overall timeout. So it only trusts idle once the renderer has truly stopped. (Confirmed `GFXC_BufferBlit` is a synchronous `memcpy`, so the canvas commit isn't the bottleneck — it's purely the tick cadence + premature check, exactly as you said.)

**2. SD not ready at boot.** `fs err 3` = `FR_NOT_READY` — the SDMMC card-detect/analysis isn't finished that early (your `sd` command works later because the card has come up by then). Added a retry loop (`SD_LOAD_ATTEMPTS=5 × SD_RETRY_MS=300`) around the load so the JPEG gets a chance once the card initializes.

Expectation on rebuild:
- The render fix alone should make the splash fill the **whole screen** (even the solid-fill fallback if SD still isn't ready) — that confirms #1.
- The SD retry should let the JPEG actually load and show the photo — confirming #2.

If after this the splash is full-screen but solid-colored (not the photo), it's purely the SD timing and we tune the retry. If it's full-screen *black* specifically, note that `Splash_Panel_0`'s `SCHEME_BACKGROUND` is probably dark — that's an MGS cosmetic, not a bug. Either way, full-screen coverage is the thing to confirm first.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-26 22:51:26Z)**_

Confirmed — and here's the sizing so you set it once:

**Set `LE_SCRATCH_BUFFER_SIZE_KB` to `4096`** (4 MB) in the MGS Graphics settings. The renderer computes `maxScratchPixels = SIZE_KB·256` (for 32bpp), so:
- 512 KB → 131,072 px (≈8 tiles for 1280×800 → your slowness)
- **4096 KB → 1,048,576 px ≥ 1,280×800 = 1,024,000 → one tile = whole screen**

(4000 KB is the exact minimum; 4096 gives margin and is a clean value.)

**RAM:** `LE_SCRATCH_BUFFER_COUNT = 1` and `LE_WIDGET_BUFFER_ENABLE = 0`, so it's a single 4 MB nocache buffer — `+3.5 MB`. Tally in `.region_nocache` (32 MB): ISC pool ~10.5 + scratch 4 + dashboard 2 + splash 4 + nav ~0.5 ≈ **21 MB, ~11 MB free**. Fits.

**Why it's the right call here, not a hack:** the real slowness isn't the tile cadence — it's that a full-screen JPEG gets **re-decoded once per scratch tile** (~8× decode). A full-screen scratch collapses that to **one decode, one render pass**. The "small scratch" exists to save RAM on RAM-constrained panels; you've got 11 MB free and full-screen 32bpp content, so trading ~3.5 MB for single-pass rendering is exactly the right tradeoff. Bonus: the dashboard (RGB565, was ~4 tiles) also becomes one pass.

A couple of notes:
- The scratch is sized for the **worst-case layer bpp** (the 32bpp splash); RGB565 layers get 2M+ px from the same buffer, so 4096 covers everything.
- With one-pass rendering, `wait_render_idle` now completes in a single frame — the 120 ms stable-idle window just adds a hair of latency and stays correct (it still guards the idle-between-frames race for any heavy one-frame paint like the dashboard). We can shrink it later if you want a snappier handoff.

Once you confirm it loads fast + full-screen, I'll record the scratch bump in the journal/`ui_compositor.md` (it's currently noted there as the deferred optimization) and we can finally circle back to the nav hamburger.

Here's the full picture:

**`XLCDC_EnableBacklight()`** does one thing: enables the LCDC's internal **PWM** generator (`LCDC_LCDEN = PWMEN`, waits on `PWMSTS`). That drives the SoC's `LCD_PWM` dimming output. It has **nothing to do with PC18** — so on this board it's the wrong knob entirely, and `UiManager_EnableBacklight()` calling it has been a no-op for the real backlight.

**The actual backlight** is `AC69T88A_BACKLIGHT_EN` = **PC18**, a GPIO output (`AC69T88A_BACKLIGHT_EN_Set()` / `_Clear()`). In the current MCC `PIO_Initialize`, PIOC `OER` has bit 18 (output-enabled) and `ODSR = 0x40000000` — **bit 18 is 0, i.e. PC18 starts low**. So the "set high on start" appears already removed from the pin config; nothing in the tree calls `_Set()`, so right now nothing ever actually turns the backlight on through software.

So the fix is to make `UiManager_EnableBacklight()` drive the real pin:

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-26 23:08:44Z)**_

Done for today. Summary of the backlight investigation and fix:

**What `XLCDC_EnableBacklight()` does:** enables the LCDC's internal PWM (`LCDC_LCDEN = PWMEN`, waits on `PWMSTS`) — i.e. the SoC's `LCD_PWM` dimming output. On this board that pin isn't wired to the backlight, so it's been a **no-op for the real backlight**. That's why my "gating" never actually gated anything.

**The real backlight** is GPIO **`AC69T88A_BACKLIGHT_EN` (PC18)**, with `_Set()`/`_Clear()` macros. Current MCC `PIO_Initialize` leaves PC18 **low** at boot (the old "set high on start" is gone from the pin config), and nothing was calling `_Set()` — so software never turned it on.

**Fix:** `UiManager_EnableBacklight()` now drives PC18 (`AC69T88A_BACKLIGHT_EN_Set()`) instead of the LCDC PWM. Combined with the pin starting low, the panel stays dark until the loader enables it after the splash is painted — which is finally the *real* "no pre-splash frame" gating.

**Two things to confirm on hardware next session** (I flagged them in the comment + journal):
1. **Polarity** — I assumed active-high (`_Set` = on). If the panel's backlight is active-low, it's a one-line flip to `_Clear()`.
2. **Nothing else forces PC18 high** (bootstrap/u-boot/hardware pull). If the panel lit in earlier tests despite PC18 being low, something external is driving it — worth a scope/check.

Also recorded the two wrap-up items in the docs: the **scratch bump** (512→4096 KB, shipped) and the **canvas-vs-layer terminology cleanup** (incl. `NAV_LAYER`→`NAV_CANVAS`), plus your notes that `NAV_CANVAS` naming and "higher level assigns the canvas→layer binding on show" are a future refactor.

Still open for next time: confirm backlight polarity on hardware, and the **nav hamburger** trace. Nothing's been committed — all changes are in the working tree for your review/build.
